<issue identifier="MM-464">
<title>Wallet has no did:web identity removal flow (UI gated to did:plc; backend would wedge on the PLC tombstone if ungated)</title>
<description>
Found during the <issue id="325ad336-792b-4581-9e45-c162dd9e26ba" href="https://linear.app/malpercio/issue/MM-395/migrate-didwebmalperciodev-to-production-staging-rehearsal-first-live">MM-395</issue> rehearsal (see `docs/validation/2026-07-24-mm-395-didweb-migration-rehearsal.md`): the wallet's permanent identity removal is did:plc-only end to end. This is the same defect class as the six rehearsal bugs — did:plc assumptions ([plc.directory](<http://plc.directory>) + tombstone op) in a surface that should be method-aware — caught here by inspection before it could bite live.

## Current state

**UI (the actual user-visible gap):** `+page.svelte` gates the entry point on `selectedDid?.startsWith('did:plc:')`, so `DIDDocumentScreen` never renders the "Remove this identity…" button for a did:web. A did:web identity cannot be removed from the wallet's removal flow at all — the gate is correct defensively, because of what sits behind it:

**Backend (latent wedge, currently unreachable from the UI):** `confirm_identity_removal` runs `deleteAccount` first (method-agnostic, would succeed), then `tombstone_and_wipe`, which fetches the DID's **[plc.directory](<http://plc.directory>) audit log** for the tombstone `prev` — a 404 for any did:web. The tombstone never submits, the local wipe (gated behind tombstone success) never runs, and the pending-removal marker never clears: the account would be gone (single-use email code spent) while the wallet re-offers a doomed "tombstone pending, retry" on every launch, forever. Unreachable today only because the UI gate exists; the raw IPC command has no did:web guard of its own.

Meanwhile the only did:web affordance is `forget_identity_locally` (local wipe, no server deletion) — designed as the escape hatch for foreign/dead accounts, not as a first-party removal flow.

## What "deletion" means for a did:web

There is no PLC tombstone. A did:web dies when its document leaves the domain — an **operator action outside the wallet's control** (delete/blank `https://<host>/.well-known/did.json`, or serve 410). So the did:web removal flow is:

1. `requestAccountDelete` / `deleteAccount` (unchanged, method-agnostic),
2. **no PLC tombstone leg** — no tombstone marker semantics, no retry state,
3. local Keychain wipe,
4. UI: tell the user the last step is theirs — take the `did.json` down to retire the DID network-wide, with the same "the wallet can't do this part for you" framing the did:web ceremony's publish step already uses.

`RemovalOutcome.tombstone_cid` becomes optional (or a variant) — there is no CID to report.

## Suggested shape

* Backend first: branch `confirm_identity_removal`/`tombstone_and_wipe` on `did:web:` (mirror of the `finalize_migration` branch from PR #420) — did:web → deleteAccount → wipe, never touching [plc.directory](<http://plc.directory>). Also guard the raw command so an ungated caller can't reproduce the wedge.
* Then ungate the UI: drop the `did:plc:` condition on `onremove` and give `RemoveIdentityScreen` a did:web epilogue ("remove your did.json to finish retiring the DID") instead of the tombstone progress state.
* Unit tests: did:web removal never calls [plc.directory](<http://plc.directory>); wipe ordering preserved; the wedge regression (marker cleared without a tombstone; no permanent retry state).

## Traceability

* Rehearsal record: `docs/validation/2026-07-24-mm-395-didweb-migration-rehearsal.md` ("every did:plc assumption broke on did:web contact" — this is the next instance)
* Sibling fixes for the same class: PR #418 (ceremony key encoding), #419 (path detection), #420 (discover_pds + finalize), #422 (service-id parsing)
* Immediate practical relevance: <issue id="325ad336-792b-4581-9e45-c162dd9e26ba" href="https://linear.app/malpercio/issue/MM-395/migrate-didwebmalperciodev-to-production-staging-rehearsal-first-live">MM-395</issue> cleanup wants the throwaway `did:web:rehersal-production.up.railway.app` account deleted on production. With no wallet flow, cleanup goes through the admin surface (server-side deletion) + `forget_identity_locally` on the device — which is fine, and this ticket is what makes the first-party path exist for real users.
</description>

# Linear Development Workflow

This skill manages the full lifecycle of working on a Linear issue: from picking it up through opening a PR.

## Starting Work on an Issue

When the user indicates they want to work on a Linear issue (e.g., "Let's work on MM-42"):

1. **Parse the issue identifier** from the user's message. The pattern is `MM-` followed by a number.

2. **Fetch the issue details** from Linear using the `get_issue` tool with the parsed identifier. Display a brief summary to the user: title, description (truncated if long), priority, and any existing labels.

3. **Update the issue in Linear:**
   - Set the status to **"In Progress"**
   - Assign it to **"me"** (the authenticated user)

   Use the `save_issue` tool with the issue's `id`, `state: "In Progress"`, and `assignee: "me"`.

4. **Create a git branch from a fresh base** using the issue's suggested branch name:
   - The `get_issue` response includes a `branchName` field — use that as the branch name.
   - **Fetch first, then branch from the remote tip — never from a possibly-stale local HEAD:**
     `git fetch origin main && git checkout -b <branchName> origin/main`
     A stale base silently duplicates work that already merged (hours lost rebuilding an already-shipped backend is the known failure mode).
   - If the branch already exists locally, check it out, then run `git log --oneline <branchName>..origin/main` and surface to the user how far behind the base is.

5. **Verify sibling work is in the base.** If the issue depends on or overlaps sibling issues already marked Done in Linear, confirm their PRs are actually present in the branch base (e.g. `git log --oneline origin/main | grep -i mm-nnn`, or check for the files/routes they added) before concluding any related feature is "missing". **"Linear says Done but the code isn't here" is a hard stop-and-verify signal — it almost always means your base is stale, not that the feature needs building.**

6. **Confirm to the user** what happened: issue assigned, status updated, branch created/checked out (and from which base commit). Then ask what they'd like to tackle first, or summarize the issue so they can dive in.

## Opening a PR (Auto-transition to "In Review")

When the user asks to open a PR, create a pull request, or you detect that a PR is being created for a branch associated with a Linear issue:

1. **Identify the Linear issue** from the current branch name. Linear branch names typically contain the issue identifier (e.g., `malpercio/mm-42-fix-the-thing`). Extract the `MM-XXX` portion.

2. **Create the PR** as the user requests (follow normal PR creation workflow).

3. **After the PR is successfully created**, update the Linear issue:
   - Set the status to **"In Review"**
   - Attach the PR URL as a link on the issue using the `links` field in `save_issue`

   Use `save_issue` with the issue's `id`, `state: "In Review"`, and `links: [{"url": "<pr-url>", "title": "Pull Request"}]`.

4. **Confirm** to the user that the issue has been moved to "In Review" and the PR link has been attached.

## Important Notes

- Always fetch the issue first to confirm it exists and get the full `id` (UUID) needed for updates.
- If the issue is already "In Progress" and assigned, skip those updates and just create the branch.
- If branch creation fails (e.g., uncommitted changes), inform the user and suggest next steps rather than silently failing.
- The PR-to-"In Review" transition should happen automatically whenever a PR is opened during a session where the user started work on a Linear issue. Track the active issue identifier throughout the session.

This is the same defect class as the six rehearsal bugs — did:plc assumptions ([plc.directory](<http://plc.directory>) + tombstone op) in a surface that should be method-aware — caught here by inspection before it could bite live.

## Current state

**UI (the actual user-visible gap):** `+page.svelte` gates the entry point on `selectedDid?.startsWith('did:plc:')`, so `DIDDocumentScreen` never renders the "Remove this identity…" button for a did:web. A did:web identity cannot be removed from the wallet's removal flow at all — the gate is correct defensively, because of what sits behind it:

**Backend (latent wedge, currently unreachable from the UI):** `confirm_identity_removal` runs `deleteAccount` first (method-agnostic, would succeed), then `tombstone_and_wipe`, which fetches the DID's **[plc.directory](<http://plc.directory>) audit log** for the tombstone `prev` — a 404 for any did:web. The tombstone never submits, the local wipe (gated behind tombstone success) never runs, and the pending-removal marker never clears: the account would be gone (single-use email code spent) while the wallet re-offers a doomed "tombstone pending, retry" on every launch, forever. Unreachable today only because the UI gate exists; the raw IPC command has no did:web guard of its own.

Meanwhile the only did:web affordance is `forget_identity_locally` (local wipe, no server deletion) — designed as the escape hatch for foreign/dead accounts, not as a first-party removal flow.

## What "deletion" means for a did:web

There is no PLC tombstone. A did:web dies when its document leaves the domain — an **operator action outside the wallet's control** (delete/blank `https://<host>/.well-known/did.json`, or serve 410). So the did:web removal flow is:

1. `requestAccountDelete` / `deleteAccount` (unchanged, method-agnostic),
2. **no PLC tombstone leg** — no tombstone marker semantics, no retry state,
3. local Keychain wipe,
4. UI: tell the user the last step is theirs — take the `did.json` down to retire the DID network-wide, with the same "the wallet can't do this part for you" framing the did:web ceremony's publish step already uses.

`RemovalOutcome.tombstone_cid` becomes optional (or a variant) — there is no CID to report.

## Suggested shape

* Backend first: branch `confirm_identity_removal`/`tombstone_and_wipe` on `did:web:` (mirror of the `finalize_migration` branch from PR #420) — did:web → deleteAccount → wipe, never touching [plc.directory](<http://plc.directory>). Also guard the raw command so an ungated caller can't reproduce the wedge.
* Then ungate the UI: drop the `did:plc:` condition on `onremove` and give `RemoveIdentityScreen` a did:web epilogue ("remove your did.json to finish retiring the DID") instead of the tombstone progress state.
* Unit tests: did:web removal never calls [plc.directory](<http://plc.directory>); wipe ordering preserved; the wedge regression (marker cleared without a tombstone; no permanent retry state).

# Obsign (identity-wallet) Mobile App

Last verified: 2026-07-08
Last updated: 2026-07-20

## Purpose

Tauri v2 iOS application — SvelteKit 2 + Svelte 5 frontend running in a native WKWebView, communicating with a Rust backend exclusively through Tauri's IPC bridge.

## Browser test harness (drive the app without a simulator)

The whole frontend runs in a plain desktop browser under `vite dev` — the only thing the
browser lacks is the Tauri `invoke()` seam, which the harness intercepts with Tauri's
official `mockIPC`. This lets an agent (or a human) reach every screen and reproduce any
state, including rare error states, without a Mac/Xcode/simulator. Design + acceptance
criteria: [docs/archive/design-plans/2026-07-12-browser-harness.md](../../docs/archive/design-plans/2026-07-12-browser-harness.md).

**Start it** (or use the `.claude/launch.json` config `wallet-harness` / `wallet-harness-proxy`):
- **Fake mode** (default, no backend needed): `pnpm --dir apps/identity-wallet dev:harness` → http://localhost:5173.
- **Proxy mode** (real thin-HTTP calls against a hermetic local PDS): in one terminal
  `cargo build -p pds` then `just harness-pds` (prints the URL + admin token); in another,
  `VITE_HARNESS_PDS_URL=<url> VITE_HARNESS_ADMIN_TOKEN=<token> pnpm --dir apps/identity-wallet dev:harness:proxy`.
- Plain `pnpm dev` never activates the harness (double-gated on `import.meta.env.DEV && VITE_HARNESS`);
  `pnpm check:harness-absence` proves it is tree-shaken out of production builds.

**`window.__harness` console API** (both modes):
- `.scenario(name)` — switch preset and reload (persists across reload). Presets:
  `fresh-install`, `foreign-pds` (a spec-compliant non-Custos host — advertises no
  capabilities, so the create flow's gate closes and steers to import),
  `unreachable-pds` (the same empty capability list, but `reached: false` — the gate must
  show a retryable error, never the steer), `one-identity`, `multi-identity`,
  `alert-active`, `migration-in-flight`,
  `agent-connected`, `app-password-minted`, plus the share-recovery matrix:
  `recover-escrow` (happy path A — iCloud Share 1 + zero-delay escrow release),
  `recover-sovereign` (happy path B — manual Share 3 entry; paste
  `state().recovery.fixtures.share3Words` or `.share3`), `recover-wrong-set`
  (`fixtures.wrongSet` → SHARE_SET_MISMATCH), `recover-corrupt-share`
  (`fixtures.corrupt` → SHARE_CHECKSUM), `recover-mismatch` (verification fails —
  shares don't match the identity), `recover-pending-delay` (24h escrow window; the
  second poll releases), `recover-cancelled` (pending release cancelled → uniform
  401 on poll), `recover-epilogue-resume` (launch resumes an interrupted rotation
  epilogue). `.scenarios` lists them.
- `.failNext(command, error)` — make the next call of `command` reject with a typed error,
  e.g. `window.__harness.failNext('create_account', { code: 'EXPIRED_CODE' })`.
- `.emit(event, payload)` — deliver a Tauri event to live `listen()` subscribers;
  `window.__harness.emit('auth_ready')` simulates the OAuth deep-link return.
- `.state()` — a read-only snapshot of the fake store. `.mode` is `'fake'` or `'proxy'`.

**Proxy mode is real only for the thin-HTTP subset** — `create_account` (mints + redeems a
real claim code, POSTs `/v1/accounts/mobile`) and `get_available_user_domains`
(describeServer). By the honest boundary, these stay **faked even in proxy mode** (heavy
Rust logic with no thin-HTTP form): the DID ceremony (`perform_did_ceremony`,
`*_did_web_ceremony`), OAuth completion (`prepare/complete_oauth_flow`), the migration
transfer legs (`transfer_repo`/`transfer_blobs`/…, `finalize_migration`), recovery/claim
PLC ops, and the agent surfaces (which need a real post-ceremony session the faked
ceremony never mints). Fidelity the browser can never cover: real Keychain/Secure-Enclave,
the biometric prompt, ASWebAuthenticationSession, WKWebView rendering, safe-area insets,
camera/QR — those stay simulator/device concerns.

**Fake handler coverage is enforced:** every command in `$lib/ipc` must have a handler in
`src/lib/harness/registry.ts` or `registry.test.ts` fails (`pnpm test`). Harness code lives
in `src/lib/harness/` (`install`/`registry`/`state`/`scenarios`/`control` + `proxy/`),
activated by `src/hooks.client.ts`.

## Contracts

### Frontend (SvelteKit 2 + Svelte 5)

**Exposes:**
- `src/lib/ipc/` — per-domain typed wrappers for all Tauri IPC commands, re-exported from `src/lib/ipc/index.ts`; import from `$lib/ipc` instead of calling `invoke()` directly. Exports: `createAccount()`, `performDIDCeremony()`, `registerHandle()`, `getAvailableUserDomains()`, `registerCreatedIdentity()`, `startOAuthFlow()`, `getPdsUrl()`, `savePdsUrl()`, `getPdsCapabilities()`/`hasPdsCapability()`, `getAppearancePreference()`, `setAppearancePreference()`, `resolveIdentity()`, `authenticateSourcePds()`, `requestClaimVerification()`, `signAndVerifyClaim()`, `submitClaim()`, `listIdentities()`, `getStoredDidDoc()`, `getDeviceKeyId()`, `checkIdentityStatus()`, `buildRecoveryOverride()`, `submitRecoveryOverride()`, and their associated types (`CreateAccountResult`, `CreateAccountError`, `DIDCeremonyResult`, `DIDCeremonyError`, `RegisterHandleResult`, `RegisterHandleError`, `RegisterIdentityError`, `OAuthError`, `PdsConfigError`, `AppearancePreference`, `AppearanceError`, `IdentityInfo`, `VerifiedClaimOp`, `OpDiff`, `ServiceChange`, `ClaimResult`, `ResolveError`, `ClaimError`, `IdentityStoreError`, `UnauthorizedChange`, `IdentityStatus`, `SignedRecoveryOp`, `RecoveryError`, `SignedMigrationOp`, `MigrateError`) and migration wrappers (`buildMigrationOp()`, `submitMigrationOp()`) and outbound-migration orchestrator wrappers (`prepareMigration()`, `authenticateMigrationSource()`, `createDestinationAccount()`, `transferRepo()`, `transferBlobs(did, acceptLoss)`, `transferPreferences()`, `verifyImport()`, `armIdentityLeg()`, `finalizeMigration()`) with types (`AccountStatus`, `PreparedMigration`, `MigrationError`, `BlobLoss`, `BlobTransferDirection`), the sovereign change-handle wrappers (`getIdentityHandleDomains()`, `changeHandle()` — biometric-gated) with type `HandleChangeError`, and identity-removal wrappers (`requestIdentityRemoval()`, `confirmIdentityRemoval()`, `tombstoneIdentity()`, `listPendingRemovals()`, `forgetIdentityLocally()`) with types (`RemovalError`, `RemovalOutcome`), and the share-recovery wrappers (`startShareRecovery()`, `addRecoveryShare()`, `removeRecoveryShare()`, `initiateEscrowRelease()`, `requestEscrowRelease()`, `verifyRecoveryShares()`, `recoverIdentity()` — biometric-gated, `runRecoveryEpilogue()`, `getPendingRecoveryEpilogue()`, `confirmRecoveryBackup()`) with types (`ShareRecoveryError`, `CollectedShare`, `RecoveryTarget`, `EscrowReleaseStatus`, `RecoveredIdentity`, `RecoveryAnchor`, `EpilogueResult`, `PendingEpilogue`), and the media-backup wrappers (`getBlobBackupStatus()`, `setBlobBackupEnabled()`, `runBlobBackup()`, `restoreBlobBackup()` — biometric-gated, and the app-global background-sweep settings `getBackgroundBackupSettings()` / `setBackgroundBackupSettings()`) with types (`BlobBackupStatus`, `BlobBackupRunReport`, `BlobRestoreReport`, `BlobFailure`, `BackupLocation`, `BlobBackupError`, `BackgroundBackupSettings`, `BackgroundBackupError`), and the repo-backup wrappers (`getRepoBackupStatus()`, `setRepoBackupEnabled()`, `runRepoBackup()`, `exportRepoBackup()` — none biometric-gated; all read the public `getRepo` or local disk) with types (`RepoBackupStatus`, `RepoBackupRunReport`, `RepoExport`, `RepoBackupError`)
- `src/lib/components/onboarding/` — one screen component per step of the create / import / recover onboarding flows (the directory listing is the authoritative inventory; hand-counted lists here drifted twice)
- `src/lib/components/home/` — the home-surface screen components (the directory listing is the authoritative inventory) plus the DIDAvatar utility component (deterministic DID-derived hue circle). ChangeHandleScreen is the sovereign change-handle surface reached from DIDDocumentScreen's "Change handle" button (did:plc + device-key-as-root only): it loads the hosting PDS's served domains, pre-flights the session (`ensureIdentitySession`, passwordless `sovereignLogin` on `NEEDS_UNLOCK`), then runs the biometric-gated `changeHandle`. AppPasswordsScreen is the app-password surface reached from DIDDocumentScreen's "Sign in to Bluesky and other apps" button: it lists/mints/revokes the account's scoped app passwords via `SessionProvider::full_access_client` (SESSION_LOCKED → `sovereignLogin` + retry; mint and revoke are biometric-gated; the generated secret is shown once with copy and never persisted). MediaBackupScreen is the user-held blob-backup surface reached from DIDDocumentScreen's "Back up media" button: opt-in with the mirror size always shown, "Back up now" (incremental, CID-verified sync pass over public sync endpoints — no session), and a biometric-gated "Restore to server" (`uploadBlob` via `SessionProvider::full_access_client`; SESSION_LOCKED → `sovereignLogin` + retry), with per-blob failures listed rather than aborting the run. The same screen also holds a "Back up your posts" section (`repo_backup.rs`): opt-in with the snapshot size + last-backup shown, and "Back up posts now" (a full-CAR `getRepo` snapshot, validated client-side before it replaces the prior copy — no session, no biometric); there is no repo "restore" button (an `importRepo` needs a deactivated account, so restore flows through migration). `+page.svelte` fires silent opportunistic `runBlobBackup` **and** `runRepoBackup` passes on app open for opted-in identities (each on its own per-DID flag). MyAgentsScreen is the agent list; AgentDetailScreen is the per-agent sub-view (audit-trail paging + biometric-gated revoke) it renders on selection, its lifetime scoped to that selection. RemoveIdentityScreen is the permanent-removal flow (warn → emailed-code + password → biometric-gated hold-to-remove → progress, with a "tombstone pending, retry" state), reached from DIDDocumentScreen's destructive `onremove`
- `src/lib/appearance.ts` — in-app appearance override (System / Light / Dark): `normalizePreference()` / `toColorScheme()` (pure, tested by `appearance.test.ts`), `readLocalMirror()`, `initAppearance()` (launch-time reconcile: re-asserts the localStorage mirror, then reads the Keychain via IPC and lets it win), `setAppearance()` (applies the inline `color-scheme` override on `<html>` instantly, writes the mirror, then persists to the Keychain). The localStorage mirror (key `appearance-preference`) exists only so `src/app.html`'s inline `<head>` script can apply a forced appearance before first paint; the Keychain is the source of truth
- `src/lib/agent-scopes.ts` — plain-language descriptions of granular OAuth scope tokens for the agent-consent surfaces: `describeScope(token)` / `describeScopes(tokens)` return `{ summary, token, elevated }` (the raw token is always shown alongside the human sentence; `account:*`/`identity:*`/full-access grants are flagged `elevated`; an unknown token falls back to showing itself, never a vague label). Tested by `agent-scopes.test.ts`
- `src/lib/deadline.ts` — PLC recovery deadline utilities: `getDeadline(createdAt)` (adds 72h to ISO 8601 timestamp), `getUrgency(deadline)` (returns `'safe'` | `'warning'` | `'critical'` | `'expired'`), `formatCountdown(deadline)` (human-readable `"Xh Ym remaining"`). `Urgency` type exported. Thresholds: expired = 0, critical < 4h, warning < 24h, safe >= 24h
- `src/routes/+page.svelte` — root page: two-flow state machine starting at `mode_select`. **Create flow:** mode_select -> pds_config -> claim_code -> email -> handle -> password (every pre-submit step wires `onback` to the previous step) -> loading -> did_ceremony -> did_success -> shamir_backup -> handle_registration -> complete -> authenticating -> home (after handle_registration succeeds, `finishCreateFlow()` calls `registerCreatedIdentity()` to persist the new identity to `IdentityStore` so it appears in `IdentityListHome` — best-effort, never blocks the flow). `pds_config` is a **capability gate**, not just a form: after `savePdsUrl` (which re-probes the host, so this reads a warm cache) it calls `getPdsCapabilities()` and, unless the host advertises `createCeremony`, routes to `create_unavailable` (`CreateUnavailableScreen`) instead of `claim_code` — the create ceremony is Custos-structural, so a standard PDS is refused before the user types an account detail rather than failing inside `/v1/accounts/mobile`. This is the one gate that reads `ServerCapabilities.reached`: it does not merely withhold a feature, it tells the user their server cannot create identities, and a host that could not be asked must produce a retryable error instead of that accusation. The gate covers both create paths, since the did:web branch also passes through `pds_config`. From `create_unavailable` the import flow is one tap away with the chosen server still configured. **Import flow:** mode_select -> identity_input -> pds_auth -> email_verification -> review_operation -> claim_success -> home. **Home:** home -> identity_detail -> { change_handle | alert_detail -> recovery_override }. On mount, checks for existing identities via `listIdentities()` and skips to `home` if any exist. Registers a `visibilitychange` listener that calls `checkIdentityStatus()` when the app returns to foreground while on the `home` step

**Guarantees:**
- SSR is disabled globally (`ssr = false` in `src/routes/+layout.ts`); the frontend is a fully static SPA loaded from disk by WKWebView
- Build output lands in `dist/` (configured via `pages: 'dist'` in `svelte.config.js`)
- Frontend calls Tauri commands only through the `src/lib/ipc/` modules (imported from `$lib/ipc`) — no raw `invoke()` calls in page components
- PDS error codes from `create_account` are mapped back to the originating screen (e.g. EXPIRED_CODE -> claim_code step, EMAIL_TAKEN -> email step)

**Expects:**
- `pnpm install` has been run in `apps/identity-wallet/`
- Node.js 22.x is in PATH (provided by the Nix dev shell)

### Rust Backend (src-tauri/)

**Exposes:**
- `src/lib.rs::create_account(claim_code, email, handle) -> Result<CreateAccountResult, CreateAccountError>` — Tauri IPC command: gets or creates device key via `device_key::get_or_create()`, POSTs to PDS `/v1/accounts/mobile`, stores tokens in Keychain on success
- `src/lib.rs::perform_did_ceremony(handle: String, password: String) -> Result<DIDCeremonyResult, DIDCeremonyError>` — Tauri IPC command running the **client-share ceremony** (ceremony inversion): fetches the PDS signing key (GET /v1/repo-signing-key), loads-or-generates the client-side share set via `share_ceremony::load_or_create` (recovery seed + `derive_recovery_keypair` + 2-of-3 v2 envelope split, staged in the `ceremony-staging` Keychain slot BEFORE any network call so a retry reuses the identical set/set_id), builds the signed did:plc genesis op via `crypto::build_did_plc_genesis_op_multi_rotation_with_external_signer` with `rotationKeys = [device, recovery, PDS]` (ADR-0027) using the device key as signer, POSTs the op + password + `recoveryKey` + `escrowShare` (the Share 2 envelope — the only share Custos ever sees) to POST /v1/dids, persists DID + upgraded session token in Keychain, writes the wallet-generated Share 1 envelope to the per-DID slot `recovery-share-1:{did}` with a read-back verify (same convention as the re-key flow, so a second identity's ceremony cannot overwrite the first's Share 1), and returns `{ did, share3, share3Words }` to the frontend
- `src/lib.rs::confirm_share_backup(did: String) -> Result<(), ShareBackupError>` — Tauri IPC command: the ceremony teardown gate. Verifies the ceremony DID's Share 1 is durably present in `recovery-share-1:{did}` (else `SHARE_NOT_STORED` — the staging slot must not be destroyed while it is the seed's only home), then deletes the `ceremony-staging` slot (the seed's and Share 2's last local copy). The `did` is threaded from the ceremony result so the check reads the exact identity just created (mirrors the re-key epilogue's `confirm_rekey`). Idempotent; invoked by the frontend when the Shamir backup screen's confirmation completes
- `src/share_ceremony.rs` — client-side share generation module: `CeremonyShareSet` (recovery key did:key + the three base32 envelope strings + the Share 3 word phrase, all share material in `Zeroizing`), `load_or_create(handle, pds_url)` (reuse a valid staged set or generate + stage a fresh one; the staging record stores the three envelopes only — the seed is recomputed via `combine_envelopes(share1, share2)` on load), `clear_staging()` (idempotent teardown), `STAGING_ACCOUNT` (`"ceremony-staging"`). **Fail-closed staging contract:** only a genuinely absent slot, or one staged for different ceremony inputs (a new handle/PDS is the user's explicit abandonment of the old attempt), permits fresh generation; a present-but-unreadable/corrupt record errors with `StagingCorrupt` and preserves the slot — it may be the exact set a prior attempt already bound to a genesis op and escrowed, so overwriting it would permanently destroy the recovery seed
- `src/share_recovery.rs` — the "Recover existing identity" ceremony (10 Tauri IPC commands), the consuming inverse of `share_ceremony.rs`: `start_share_recovery(identifier)` (resolve handle/did:plc via plc.directory, then auto-load Share 1 from the resolved DID's per-DID slot `recovery-share-1:{did}`, falling back to the legacy global `recovery-share-1`, when it holds a valid v2 envelope), `add_recovery_share(share)` (base32 or word-phrase entry; SHARE_CHECKSUM, SHARE_SET_MISMATCH — with both set_ids — and DUPLICATE_SHARE are distinct, pre-combine errors), `remove_recovery_share(index)`, the escrow-assisted path client `initiate_escrow_release()` / `request_escrow_release(otp?)` (targets the account's own PDS endpoint from the authoritative DID state; OTP opens the release, OTP-less calls poll the pending window; the server's uniform 401 maps to RELEASE_UNAUTHORIZED), `verify_recovery_shares()` (combine → `derive_recovery_keypair` → compare against the **authoritative plc.directory audit log**, never a cached doc — mismatch is SHARES_DO_NOT_MATCH_IDENTITY, before anything signs), `recover_identity()` (fresh per-DID device key; the recovery key signs the rotation op installing it at `rotationKeys[0]`; talks ONLY to plc.directory — the fully-sovereign path makes zero PDS requests until re-escrow; idempotent on retry; durably stages the epilogue before returning), `run_recovery_epilogue(skip_escrow?)` (resumable: swap the new recovery key into `rotationKeys[1]` signed by the new device key → re-escrow the new Share 2 over a stored-or-fresh device-key sovereign session → rewrite the recovered DID's per-DID slot `recovery-share-1:{did}` with read-back verify; each step recorded in the durable `recovery-epilogue` Keychain record as it completes), `get_pending_recovery_epilogue()` (launch-time resume hook), `confirm_recovery_backup()` (teardown gate mirroring `confirm_share_backup`; destroys the epilogue record only after the NEW Share 1 is verified durable in the per-DID slot). Session state (`AppState.share_recovery_state`) is in-memory by design — the pre-anchor phase restarts from the entry screen; only the epilogue persists. `ShareRecoveryError` serializes as `{ code: "SCREAMING_SNAKE_CASE" }` with camelCase fields
- `src/lib.rs::{prepare_did_web_ceremony,complete_did_web_ceremony}` — did:web sibling ceremony: obtains the same device key and pending account's reserved repo key, lets the frontend compose/export the reviewed `did.json`, then submits it to `POST /v1/dids` only after it is externally resolvable. Completion persists the upgraded session and the server-returned Shamir Share 1 into the per-DID slot `recovery-share-1:{did}` (the same convention as the client-share and re-key paths); managed-hosting selection then opts the account into `/v1/did-web/hosting`.
- `src/oauth.rs` — OAuth PKCE client module: `AppState` (pending_login + oauth_session mutexes + custos_client OnceLock + pds_client + claim_state + recovery_state + migration_state + orchestration_state; both source logins — the claim flow and the outbound migration — are password-based `createSession`, so neither parks OAuth state — see `claim::authenticate_source_pds` / `migration_orchestrator::authenticate_migration_source`), `OAuthSession` (access/refresh/expiry/nonce), `DPoPKeypair` (P-256, persisted in Keychain), `OAuthError` enum, PKCE utilities (verifier + S256 challenge), `OAuthPrepared` (the `{authUrl, callbackScheme}` returned to the frontend), `prepare_oauth_flow` + `complete_oauth_flow` (the create-flow login split around the in-app auth session: prepare does DPoP keygen/PKCE/PAR → authorize URL and parks the verifier+CSRF in `pending_login`; complete validates the callback URL + does the token exchange), `parse_callback_url` (shared callback-URL parser, `pub(crate)`); `AppState::pds_client()` accessor exposes `PdsClient` for claim flow commands
- `src/claim.rs` — PLC rotation key claim flow module (5 Tauri IPC commands): `resolve_identity(handle_or_did) -> Result<IdentityInfo, ResolveError>` (resolves handle/DID to identity info via plc.directory, stores ClaimState), `authenticate_source_pds(did, identifier, password, auth_factor_token?) -> Result<(), ClaimError>` (**password `createSession`** against the source PDS → full-session Bearer `OAuthClient` stored in ClaimState; the next steps are PLC/identity ops that no OAuth `transition:generic` token can drive, so a full session is required — ADR-0021/MM-289; the password is used once and never stored. An email-2FA account returns `TwoFactorRequired` on the token-less attempt — the PDS emails a code and the UI re-invokes with `auth_factor_token`), `request_claim_verification(did) -> Result<(), ClaimError>` (calls `requestPlcOperationSignature` XRPC on old PDS to trigger email verification), `sign_and_verify_claim(did, token) -> Result<VerifiedClaimOp, ClaimError>` (calls `getRecommendedDidCredentials` and `signPlcOperation` on old PDS, fetches audit log, verifies signature + 4-point local checks, stores signed op in ClaimState), `submit_claim(did) -> Result<ClaimResult, ClaimError>` (POSTs signed op to plc.directory, persists identity to IdentityStore, clears ClaimState). Types: `IdentityInfo`, `VerifiedClaimOp`, `OpDiff`, `ServiceChange`, `ClaimResult`, `ClaimState`. Error enums: `ResolveError` (HANDLE_NOT_FOUND, DID_NOT_FOUND, PDS_UNREACHABLE, NETWORK_ERROR), `ClaimError` (INVALID_TOKEN, VERIFICATION_FAILED, PLC_DIRECTORY_ERROR, UNAUTHORIZED, SOURCE_AUTH_FAILED, TWO_FACTOR_REQUIRED, ACCOUNT_MISMATCH, INSECURE_SOURCE_URL, INSUFFICIENT_SCOPE, RATE_LIMITED, SERVER_ERROR, NETWORK_ERROR)
- `src/oauth_client.rs` — `OAuthClient`: authenticated HTTP client supporting two auth modes selected at construction (private `AuthMode` enum): `new(session, base_url)` builds a **DPoP** client (wraps every request with `Authorization: DPoP {access_token}` + a `DPoP` proof header, transparent lazy refresh when the token has <60s remaining, automatic retry on `use_dpop_nonce` 400 responses); `new_bearer(access_jwt, refresh_jwt, base_url)` builds a **Bearer** client (`Authorization: Bearer {access_jwt}`, no DPoP proof/nonce dance, expiry derived from the access JWT's `exp` claim) — used for the migration destination-PDS session, which is created via a service-auth `createAccount` rather than an OAuth flow. Methods: `get(path)`, `post(path, body)` (JSON), `post_no_body(path)` (zero bytes, no `Content-Type` — for no-input XRPC procedures like `requestPlcOperationSignature`/`activateAccount`, whose lexicons define no input; a spec-strict PDS rejects any body — MM-291), `post_bytes(path, content_type, body)` (raw byte body — CAR repo import + blob upload)
- `src/device_key.rs` — P-256 device key management with `#[cfg]`-based dispatch: macOS/simulator uses software keys via `crypto` crate + Keychain storage; real iOS device uses Secure Enclave via `security-framework`. Public API: `get_or_create() -> Result<DevicePublicKey, DeviceKeyError>` (idempotent), `sign(data) -> Result<Vec<u8>, DeviceKeyError>`. Exposes `pub(crate)` account-name consts `DEVICE_KEY_PRIV_ACCOUNT` / `DEVICE_KEY_PUB_ACCOUNT` / `DEVICE_KEY_APP_LABEL_ACCOUNT` (single source of truth for the global device-key Keychain accounts; copied into per-DID slots by `IdentityStore::adopt_global_device_key`)
- `src/keychain.rs` — iOS Keychain abstraction (`store_item`, `get_item`, `delete_item`) under service `"ezpds-identity-wallet"`; PDS URL helpers: `store_pds_url`/`load_pds_url` (PDS base URL); OAuth helpers: `store_dpop_key`/`load_dpop_key` (P-256 DPoP private key scalar), `store_oauth_tokens`/`load_oauth_tokens` (access + refresh token pair)
- `src/http.rs` — `CustosClient` with runtime-configurable base URL (initialized via `AppState::set_custos_client(url)` on first launch; localhost:8080 debug fallback); methods: `post()`, `get()`, `post_with_bearer()`, `par()` (POST /oauth/par with DPoP proof), `token_exchange()` (POST /oauth/token with PKCE verifier); response types: `ParResponse`, `TokenResponse`, `TokenErrorResponse`
- `src/identity_store.rs` — `IdentityStore` unit struct for multi-identity Keychain management with per-DID namespacing. Public API: `add_identity(did)` (registers DID in managed-dids index), `remove_identity(did)` (deletes DID and all per-DID entries), `list_identities()` (returns managed DIDs), `get_or_create_device_key(did)` (lazy per-DID P-256 key generation), `adopt_global_device_key(did)` (aliases the per-DID device key to the global `device_key.rs` key by copying its Keychain material into the per-DID slot — used by the create flow, whose genesis op is signed with the global key before the DID exists), `store_did_doc(did, json)` / `get_did_doc(did)` (DID document persistence), `store_plc_log(did, json)` / `get_plc_log(did)` (PLC audit log persistence), and `store_oauth_tokens(did, record)` / `load_oauth_tokens(did)` / `delete_oauth_tokens(did)` for the versioned full-access Bearer session in `{did}:oauth-tokens`. All methods require DID to be registered first (returns `IdentityNotFound` otherwise). `IdentityStoreError` enum: IDENTITY_NOT_FOUND, IDENTITY_ALREADY_EXISTS, KEYCHAIN_ERROR, KEY_GENERATION_FAILED, SERIALIZATION_ERROR (serialized as `{ code: "SCREAMING_SNAKE_CASE" }`)
- `src/sovereign_session.rs` — per-DID Custos sovereign login: discovers the selected DID's current PDS and server DID, signs the shared canonical envelope with that DID's device key, validates the response DID and JWT subject/audience, persists a versioned `SovereignTokenRecord`, and exposes `stored_bearer_client(did)` for authenticated XRPC helpers. `sovereign_login` is the narrow Tauri command; the typed frontend `sovereignLogin(did)` wrapper performs the biometric gate before invoking it. The `pub(crate)` JWT/audience helpers (`bearer_jwt_claims`, `audience_matches_server`) are the single source of the sub/aud binding check, reused by `session_provider`.
- `src/session_provider.rs` — per-DID full-access **session lifecycle** (the seam every authenticated Custos-hosted operation goes through; MM-305's minimum contract). `SessionProvider::full_access_client(pds_client, store, did, now) -> Result<ActiveSession, SessionError>` runs a decision ladder under a per-DID coalescing lock: (1) no record / dead refresh → `NeedsUnlock{NoRefreshChain}`; (2) access JWT still valid (`exp > now + 120s`) → rebuild a Bearer client **with no network** (this is what makes a restart or offline launch with a live token need no prompt); (3) near-expiry with a live refresh → discover the DID's current PDS, and if the host moved **discard the old-audience record** + `NeedsUnlock{HostChanged}`, else call `com.atproto.server.refreshSession` exactly once and atomically persist the rotated pair (re-validating sub/aud). Distinct terminal errors, never looped: `NeedsUnlock{reason}`, `RateLimited{retryAfter}`, `UnsupportedHost`, `Offline{message}`, `ServerFailure{status}`, `Keychain`, `InvalidResponse`. A revoked refresh (400/401) and a host change both delete the dead record; a rate limit keeps it. Coalescing is a re-read (not a shared future): the second caller for one DID waits on the lock, then re-loads the freshly-persisted record — so a refresh token can never be raced into replay detection. Does NOT reuse `OAuthClient::refresh_token_bearer` (which is in-memory-only by design) — the provider owns refresh+persist. Types: `ActiveSession` { client, did, pds_url, access_expires_at, refresh_expires_at, rotated }, `SessionReady` (serializable summary, drops the client), `UnlockReason` (NO_REFRESH_CHAIN / REFRESH_REVOKED / HOST_CHANGED), `SessionError` (SCREAMING_SNAKE_CASE `code`). The coalescing lock registry is a process-global `OnceLock<Mutex<HashMap<did, Arc<tokio::Mutex>>>>` (unit-struct-over-global shape, like `IdentityStore`).
- `src/pds_client.rs` — PDS discovery and OAuth module for arbitrary PDS endpoints (not just our PDS). `PdsClient` struct (stateless, wraps a `reqwest::Client` + plc.directory URL). Public API: `plc_directory_url() -> &str` (returns the plc.directory base URL), `client() -> &Client` (returns the inner reqwest client), `resolve_handle(handle) -> Result<String, PdsClientError>` (DNS TXT `_atproto.{handle}` with HTTP `/.well-known/atproto-did` fallback), `discover_pds(did) -> Result<(String, PlcDidDocument), PdsClientError>` (fetches DID doc from plc.directory, extracts `atproto_pds` endpoint, verifies reachability via HEAD), `discover_auth_server(pds_url) -> Result<AuthServerMetadata, PdsClientError>` (fetches `/.well-known/oauth-authorization-server`, validates `code` response type + S256 challenge method), `pds_par(metadata, pkce_challenge, state, dpop_proof, dpop_jkt, login_hint?) -> Result<PdsParResponse, PdsClientError>` (PAR to arbitrary PDS), `pds_token_exchange(metadata, code, pkce_verifier, dpop_proof) -> Result<reqwest::Response, PdsClientError>` (returns raw response for caller nonce-retry), `build_pds_authorize_url(metadata, request_uri, login_hint?) -> String` (constructs browser redirect URL), `fetch_audit_log(did) -> Result<String, PdsClientError>` (fetches PLC operation audit log as raw JSON from `{plc_directory_url}/{did}/log/audit`), `post_plc_operation(did, operation) -> Result<(), PdsClientError>` (POSTs signed PLC operation JSON to `{plc_directory_url}/{did}`), `describe_server(pds_url) -> Result<DescribeServerResponse, PdsClientError>` (GET `com.atproto.server.describeServer` — probes an arbitrary PDS for its `did`/available-user-domains before migration, and records the response's optional `custos` capability extension into `pds_capabilities`'s per-host cache), `create_session(pds_url, identifier, password, auth_factor_token?) -> Result<CreateSessionResponse, PdsClientError>` (POST `com.atproto.server.createSession` — the claim flow's password source login; a 401 maps to `PdsClientError::InvalidCredentials`, or `AuthFactorTokenRequired` when the account has email 2FA and no code was supplied; the returned JWTs feed `OAuthClient::new_bearer`). Module-level XRPC functions (take `&OAuthClient`): the claim helpers `request_plc_operation_signature(client)`, `sign_plc_operation(client, request)`, `get_recommended_did_credentials(client)`; and the outbound-migration helpers `get_service_auth(client, aud, lxm)`, `create_account_migration(client, request)` (maps HTTP 409 → `PdsClientError::DidAlreadyExists` for resume), `import_repo(client, car_bytes)`, `upload_blob(client, mime, bytes)`, `list_missing_blobs(client, cursor)`, `get_preferences(client)`, `put_preferences(client, prefs)`, `check_account_status(client)`, `activate_account(client)`, `deactivate_account(client)`. Every authenticated XRPC helper routes its non-2xx branch through the private `classify_xrpc_response(context, resp)` (→ pure `classify_xrpc_error(status, retry_after, body)`), so a server response is classified by status — `429 → RateLimited{retry_after}`, `401 → Unauthorized`, else `XrpcError{status, error, message}` carrying the atproto error envelope — instead of being flattened into `NetworkError` (MM-290). `NetworkError` is now transport-only. Types: `PlcDidDocument` (Clone), `PlcService` (Clone), `AuthServerMetadata`, `PdsParResponse`, `SignPlcOperationRequest`, `SignPlcOperationResponse`, `RecommendedCredentials`, plus migration types `DescribeServerResponse`, `ServiceAuthToken`, `CreateAccountMigrationRequest`, `CreateAccountResponse`, `CreateSessionResponse`, `MissingBlob`/`MissingBlobs`, `UploadBlobResponse`, `AccountStatus` (from `checkAccountStatus`). `PdsClientError` enum: HANDLE_NOT_FOUND, DID_NOT_FOUND, PDS_UNREACHABLE, NETWORK_ERROR, RATE_LIMITED, UNAUTHORIZED, XRPC_ERROR, INVALID_RESPONSE, OAUTH_FAILED, DID_ALREADY_EXISTS, INVALID_CREDENTIALS, AUTH_FACTOR_TOKEN_REQUIRED, INSECURE_PDS_URL (serialized as `{ code: "SCREAMING_SNAKE_CASE" }`)
- `src/plc_monitor.rs` — PLC monitoring module: `PlcMonitor` (borrows `PdsClient`; `check_all()` iterates all managed DIDs, `check_for_changes(did)` diffs current audit log against cached log and classifies new entries as authorized/unauthorized by verifying signatures against the device key); `run_monitoring_loop(app_handle)` (spawned once at app startup, checks every 15 minutes via `tokio::time::interval` with `MissedTickBehavior::Delay`, emits `"plc_alert"` Tauri event to frontend when unauthorized changes detected); `check_identity_status` (Tauri IPC command: synchronous foreground check of all managed identities, returns `Vec<IdentityStatus>`). Types: `UnauthorizedChange` { cid, created_at, signing_key, operation } (camelCase serialization), `IdentityStatus` { did, alert_count, unauthorized_changes } (camelCase serialization), `MonitorError` { NetworkError, IdentityStoreError, ParseError } (SCREAMING_SNAKE_CASE tag serialization)
- `src/agents.rs` — Agent consent + audit module (5 **per-identity** Tauri IPC commands, the wallet side of the auth.md claim ceremony + "My agents"): `preview_agent_claim(did, user_code) -> AgentClaimPreview` (POST `/v1/agents/claim-preview` — what approving would grant, shown before the biometric gate), `confirm_agent_claim(did, user_code) -> AgentClaimConfirmation` (POST `/agent/identity/claim/confirm` — the human gate; the frontend wraps it in `authenticateBiometric()`), `list_agents(did) -> Vec<AgentSummary>`, `revoke_agent(did, registration_id)`, `get_agent_audit(did, registration_id, cursor?) -> AgentAuditPage`. Each takes a `did` and resolves a **refreshable per-DID full-access session** via `SessionProvider::full_access_client` (like `app_passwords.rs`) — issuing the request through `session.client` (`OAuthClient`), so an expired session self-heals via `refreshSession` or, failing that, `SESSION_LOCKED{reason}` cues the frontend to run the biometric `sovereignLogin(did)` and retry. This replaces the previous auth on the never-refreshed global `"session-token"`, whose lapse dead-ended every agent command as a bogus connection error. Request cores are `_impl` functions taking `&OAuthClient`, tested against httpmock. `AgentsError` (NOT_AUTHENTICATED, CODE_NOT_FOUND, CODE_EXPIRED, ALREADY_CLAIMED, ACCESS_DENIED, AGENT_NOT_FOUND, RATE_LIMITED, SESSION_LOCKED, NETWORK_ERROR, UNKNOWN) serialized as `{ code: "SCREAMING_SNAKE_CASE" }`; the ceremony's `{error}` codes map onto it in `map_ceremony_error`, and a session-lifecycle failure via `map_session_error` (only a genuine transport failure is NETWORK_ERROR — a NeedsUnlock is SESSION_LOCKED, every other verdict is UNKNOWN), so denial/expiry/lock render as explicit states
- `src/oauth_consent.rs` — Wallet-confirmed OAuth consent client (3 **per-identity** Tauri IPC commands, the wallet side of the pending-authorization primitive — Phases A + B of the wallet-confirmed-OAuth-consent design plan): `preview_oauth_consent(did, user_code) -> ConsentPreview` (resolves the selected DID's hosting PDS via `discover_pds`, `GET /oauth/authorize/consent-request?user_code=…` — what approving would grant: client name/id, redirect URI, requesting origin/IP, requested scope list, `login_hint` — shown before the biometric gate), `preview_oauth_consent_by_request_id(did, request_id) -> ConsentPreview` (Phase B QR-scan path: same preview, queried on the `request_id` dimension — the wallet extracts only the `request_id` from the scanned QR and re-verifies it server-side, never trusting QR contents for display; both share one `preview_oauth_consent_impl(did, query_key, query_value)` core), and `confirm_oauth_consent(did, request_id, client_id, decision, granted_scope) -> ConsentDecision` (signs the canonical `crypto::encode_oauth_consent_envelope` — server DID from `describe_server`, account DID, per-DID device key, `request_id`, `client_id`, decision, granted-scope hash, timestamp, nonce — with the DID's device key and POSTs `/oauth/authorize/approve`). Mirrors `sovereign_session.rs` exactly (per-DID key resolved before any request, `pds_url_is_safe`, DID-doc match); the frontend gates `confirmOAuthConsent` behind `authenticateBiometric()`, so a cancelled prompt signs and sends nothing. Request cores are `_impl` functions taking `&PdsClient`, tested against httpmock. `ConsentError` (IDENTITY_NOT_FOUND, UNSUPPORTED_HOST, REQUEST_NOT_FOUND, APPROVAL_REJECTED, ALREADY_RESOLVED, RATE_LIMITED, TRANSPORT_FAILURE, KEYCHAIN_FAILURE, SIGNING_FAILED, DID_MISMATCH, SERVER_MISMATCH, INVALID_RESPONSE, SERVER_FAILURE) serialized as `{ code: "SCREAMING_SNAKE_CASE" }` with camelCase fields
- `src/app_passwords.rs` — App-password management (3 Tauri IPC commands — the "sign the official Bluesky app into a passwordless sovereign account" surface): `create_app_password(did, name, privileged) -> AppPasswordCreated` (mints via `com.atproto.server.createAppPassword`; the returned secret is surfaced ONCE — the frontend gates the call behind `authenticateBiometric()`), `list_app_passwords(did) -> Vec<AppPasswordEntry>` (metadata only), `revoke_app_password(did, name)` (server deletes the credential + its sessions/refresh tokens atomically). All three resolve a per-DID full-access session via `SessionProvider::full_access_client` (the PDS routes require full access — an app password cannot manage app passwords); a `NeedsUnlock` maps to `SESSION_LOCKED{reason}`, the frontend's cue to run `sovereignLogin(did)` and retry, mirroring `handle_change.rs`. Thin XRPC wrappers + response types (`AppPasswordCreated`, `AppPasswordEntry`) live in `pds_client.rs`; a 409 duplicate name maps to `DUPLICATE_NAME`. `AppPasswordsError` (SESSION_LOCKED, RATE_LIMITED, DUPLICATE_NAME, IDENTITY_NOT_FOUND, SERVER_ERROR, NETWORK_ERROR)
- `src/blob_backup.rs` — User-held blob backup (4 Tauri IPC commands — the "Back up media" surface): `get_blob_backup_status(did)` (mirror location + opt-in flag + mirror size), `set_blob_backup_enabled(did, enabled)`, `run_blob_backup(did)` (incremental sync pass: paginated public `com.atproto.sync.listBlobs` → diff against the manifest → `getBlob` with Content-Type capture → **recompute the CIDv1 raw-codec SHA-256 CID and compare before writing** → atomic temp-file+rename write into `{root}/blobs/{cid}` → append to the per-DID manifest `{root}/manifests/{sanitized-did}.json` (`cid, mimeType, size, fetchedAt`), saved after every blob so an interrupted run resumes; per-blob failures land in the report, never abort the run), and `restore_blob_backup(did)` (walk the manifest, re-verify each file's hash, `uploadBlob` with the stored MIME type over a `SessionProvider::full_access_client` session — `NeedsUnlock` maps to `SESSION_LOCKED`, the biometric-`sovereignLogin` retry cue; an undownloaded iCloud placeholder or corrupt file is a per-blob failure with guidance). The mirror root resolves: `EZPDS_BLOB_BACKUP_DIR` env override (tests/dev) → the iCloud Drive ubiquity container `Documents/` on iOS (`NSFileManager.URLForUbiquityContainerIdentifier` via `objc2-foundation`, iOS-only target dep; user-visible in the Files app) → on a real device with iCloud off, `BACKUP_UNAVAILABLE` (never a silent local fallback) → elsewhere (macOS/simulator) a local app-data dir reported as `location: "local"`. A corrupt manifest is fail-closed (`MANIFEST_CORRUPT`, file preserved — it may be the only record of MIME types for bytes the PDS has lost). `BlobBackupError` (BACKUP_UNAVAILABLE, SESSION_LOCKED, RATE_LIMITED, IDENTITY_NOT_FOUND, PLC_DIRECTORY_ERROR, SERVER_ERROR, NETWORK_ERROR, STORAGE_ERROR, MANIFEST_CORRUPT, KEYCHAIN_ERROR)
- `src/repo_backup.rs` — User-held repo backup (4 Tauri IPC commands — the "Back up your posts" section of the Media Backup screen, sibling of `blob_backup.rs`): `get_repo_backup_status(did)` (location + opt-in flag + snapshot size/rev), `set_repo_backup_enabled(did, enabled)`, `run_repo_backup(did)` (a full-CAR snapshot pass: `discover_pds` → `PdsClient::fetch_repo_car` over public `com.atproto.sync.getRepo` (`auth: none`, no session) → **validate the CAR client-side** (framing + every block hashing to its CID + exactly one root + a signed commit `version==3` bound to this DID + an intact MST walk — the client twin of `repo-engine`'s `car_import`, using the pure `cid`/`ipld-core`/`serde_ipld_dagcbor` primitives, NOT the repo-engine crate; the MST walk follows subtree + record-value links but never descends into records, since records link to out-of-CAR blobs) → atomic temp-file+rename write into `{root}/repo/{sanitized-did}.car` + a versioned manifest `{root}/repo/{sanitized-did}.json` (`rootCid, rev, sizeBytes, lastBackupAt`); idempotent — an unchanged `rev` skips the CAR rewrite and only advances the timestamp), and `export_repo_backup(did)` (read + **re-validate** the stored CAR; returns `{rootCid, rev, sizeBytes, lastBackupAt, carBase64}` for a caller to import — there is deliberately no "push to my live PDS" button, since `importRepo` needs a *deactivated* account, so restore flows through the migration machinery). A `pub(crate) mirror_repo_car(root, did) -> Option<Vec<u8>>` helper (the repo twin of `blob_backup::mirror_fallback_blob`, fail-closed re-validation) is the iCloud-mirror repo source consumed both by the normal outbound migration's `migration_orchestrator::transfer_repo` (source-`getRepo`-failure fallback) and by the sovereign disaster-recovery flow (`disaster_recovery::recovery_transfer_repo`). Reuses `blob_backup::resolve_backup_root`/`BackupLocation`/`sanitize_did` and the shared ubiquity container (no new entitlement). No encryption (the repo is public data on an `auth: none` endpoint) and, unlike the blob restore, no session — so `RepoBackupError` has **no `SESSION_LOCKED`**: (BACKUP_UNAVAILABLE, RATE_LIMITED, IDENTITY_NOT_FOUND, PLC_DIRECTORY_ERROR, SERVER_ERROR, NETWORK_ERROR, STORAGE_ERROR, MANIFEST_CORRUPT, CAR_INVALID, KEYCHAIN_ERROR)
- `src/recovery.rs` — Recovery override module: `build_recovery_override(pds_client, did, unauthorized_op_cid) -> Result<SignedRecoveryOp, RecoveryError>` (fetches audit log, identifies fork point, builds counter-operation restoring pre-unauthorized state, signs with per-DID device key), `submit_recovery_override(pds_client, did, signed_op) -> Result<ClaimResult, RecoveryError>` (POSTs to plc.directory, updates cached log and DID doc); Tauri IPC commands: `build_recovery_override_cmd`, `submit_recovery_override_cmd`. Types: `SignedRecoveryOp` { diff, signed_op }, `RecoveryState` { did, signed_op }, `RecoveryError` (RECOVERY_WINDOW_EXPIRED, SIGNING_FAILED, PLC_DIRECTORY_ERROR, NETWORK_ERROR, IDENTITY_NOT_FOUND, UNAUTHORIZED_CHANGE_NOT_FOUND)
- `src/identity_removal.rs` — Permanent identity removal (5 Tauri IPC commands): `request_identity_removal(did)` (gets a full-access session via `SessionProvider::full_access_client` — a `NeedsUnlock` maps to `SessionRequired` so the UI runs `sovereignLogin` first — then calls `com.atproto.server.requestAccountDelete`, which emails a single-use code), `confirm_identity_removal(did, password, token)` (calls `deleteAccount` FIRST — a bad password/code is `InvalidToken` with nothing mutated — then persists a durable pending-removal marker and runs `tombstone_and_wipe`), `tombstone_identity(did)` (resume path: tombstone + wipe only, for when `confirm` deleted the account but the tombstone/wipe failed and the single-use code is already spent), and `list_pending_removals()` (the launch-reconciliation source: the DIDs whose post-delete tombstone/wipe never finished), and `forget_identity_locally(did)` (the local-only escape hatch: wipes the DID's Keychain material and clears any pending marker with NO network step, returning `wasLastIdentity`. For an identity whose PDS account no longer exists — deleted from another device, purged server-side, or migrated away — `deleteAccount` can only answer with an opaque 401 indistinguishable from a wrong password (the PDS is not an account-existence oracle, see `crates/pds/src/routes/delete_account.rs`), so the request/confirm flow can never make progress. It deliberately does NOT tombstone the did:plc — the DID may already be retired or now live on another PDS — so it only promises to remove the identity from THIS device; biometric-gated in the frontend). Shared core `tombstone_and_wipe` fetches the audit-log head as `prev`, builds+signs a `crypto::build_did_plc_tombstone_op` with `per_did_sign_closure` (self-verified via `verify_plc_tombstone_op`), POSTs it to plc.directory, and ONLY THEN calls `IdentityStore::remove_identity` — the wipe deletes the device key that signs the tombstone, so a submit failure must leave it intact for a retry (the `submit_then_wipe` ordering is unit-tested). **Post-delete recovery marker:** the instant `deleteAccount` succeeds, `confirm_identity_removal` records the DID in the durable `pending-removals` Keychain index (a JSON array), *before* the tombstone's network round trip — the step iOS is most likely to interrupt by suspending the app. Both `confirm_identity_removal` and `tombstone_identity` clear the marker (best-effort) once `tombstone_and_wipe` completes. On launch the UI calls `list_pending_removals()` and, for any listed DID, resumes straight to the idempotent tombstone retry rather than the request flow — which would fail against the already-deleted account. No PDS/DB changes: both `requestAccountDelete`/`deleteAccount` endpoints already exist, and the did:plc tombstone is the DID-level network messaging the PDS can't do (it holds no rotation key, ADR-0001). Types: `RemovalOutcome` { tombstoneCid, wasLastIdentity }, `RemovalError` (SESSION_REQUIRED, REQUEST_DELETE_FAILED, INVALID_TOKEN, ACCOUNT_DELETE_FAILED, INVALID_AUDIT_LOG, TOMBSTONE_SIGNING_FAILED, PLC_DIRECTORY_ERROR, IDENTITY_NOT_FOUND, LOCAL_WIPE_FAILED, RATE_LIMITED, NETWORK_ERROR)
- `src/migrate.rs` — Self-signed account-migration identity leg (ADR-0002 path 1): builds and locally device-key-signs the DID-repointing PLC op and submits it directly to plc.directory — no email token, no `signPlcOperation` round-trip. `build_migration_op(pds_client, dest_client, did) -> Result<SignedMigrationOp, MigrateError>` (fetches audit log for `prev` + current state, reads `getRecommendedDidCredentials` from the DESTINATION PDS via the passed-in authed `OAuthClient`, assembles the op with the device key preserved at `rotationKeys[0]`, runs the strict pre-sign guard, signs with the per-DID device key), `submit_migration_op(pds_client, did, signed_op) -> Result<ClaimResult, MigrateError>` (POSTs to plc.directory, refreshes cached log + DID doc); Tauri IPC commands: `build_migration_op_cmd`, `submit_migration_op_cmd`. Pure helpers: `guard_migration_op` (strict allowlist), `recommended_verification_methods`/`recommended_services` (RecommendedCredentials JSON → typed maps), `latest_op_state` (current state from newest non-nullified audit entry), `build_migration_diff`. Types: `SignedMigrationOp` { diff, signed_op }, `MigrationState` { did, dest_oauth_client, signed_op }, `MigrationInputs`; `MigrateError` (WALLET_NOT_AUTHORIZED, GUARD_REJECTED, INVALID_RECOMMENDED_CREDENTIALS, INVALID_AUDIT_LOG, SIGNING_FAILED, PLC_DIRECTORY_ERROR, NETWORK_ERROR, IDENTITY_NOT_FOUND, MIGRATION_NOT_READY). The destination-PDS OAuth login is NOT owned here — the migration orchestrator authenticates and populates `MigrationState.dest_oauth_client` before `build_migration_op_cmd` runs
- `src/migration_orchestrator.rs` — wallet-authorized outbound migration state machine (ADR-0002 path 1). Fine-grained per-step Tauri commands driving the source→dest transfer: `prepare_migration` (resolve dest describeServer + source; returns `PreparedMigration { handle, sourcePdsUrl }` for the source-auth screen), `authenticate_migration_source` (password `createSession` → full-session Bearer client, mirrors `claim::authenticate_source_pds`; per ADR-0021/MM-302 a full session is required to mint the source's `createAccount` service-auth token — HTTPS + account-match guards + email-2FA, password used once and never stored), `create_destination_account` (reserveSigningKey → getServiceAuth → deactivated `createAccount` → Bearer session; tolerates `DidAlreadyExists` for resume), `transfer_repo` (getRepo → importRepo; on a source `getRepo` failure it falls back to the local iCloud repo mirror `repo_backup::mirror_repo_car` when that mirror holds a CID/commit-valid snapshot for the DID, else surfaces the original source failure unchanged — the repo twin of the blob drain's mirror fallback), `transfer_blobs` (cursor-paginated `listMissingBlobs` drain), `transfer_preferences` (get→put), `verify_import` (`checkAccountStatus` completeness gate; returns `AccountStatus`), `arm_identity_leg` (populate `migrate::MigrationState.dest_oauth_client`, then run `migrate::build_migration_op_cmd`/`submit_migration_op_cmd`), `finalize_migration` (the safe cutover — **activate dest → mint + persist the destination sovereign session → deactivate source → Finalized**; the source stays active until the durable credential is stored, so a crash or retry never strands the account credential-less). Pure cores split out for testability (`ensure_phase_did` gate, `create_destination_account_impl`, `drain_missing_blobs`, `transfer_repo_impl`, `transfer_preferences_impl`, `import_reconciles`, `activate_destination_account`/`deactivate_source_account` cutover halves, `ensure_sovereign_session_persisted` (idempotent skip when a persisted record's refresh token is still unexpired, else `sovereign_session::sovereign_login_impl` → persist), and the `*_core` mutex-parameterized command cores; `finalize_migration_core` takes an injected `ensure_session` step so its activate → session → deactivate ordering is unit-testable without a Keychain or live PDS). `MigrationError` (MIGRATION_NOT_READY, DESTINATION_UNREACHABLE, SOURCE_AUTH_FAILED, TWO_FACTOR_REQUIRED, ACCOUNT_MISMATCH, INSECURE_SOURCE_URL, RATE_LIMITED, SERVER_ERROR, SERVICE_AUTH_FAILED, ACCOUNT_CREATION_FAILED, DESTINATION_CONFLICT, REPO_TRANSFER_FAILED, BLOB_TRANSFER_FAILED, PREFERENCES_TRANSFER_FAILED, VERIFICATION_INCOMPLETE, ACTIVATION_FAILED, SOVEREIGN_LOGIN_FAILED, SESSION_PERSIST_FAILED, DEACTIVATION_FAILED, NETWORK_ERROR — SOVEREIGN_LOGIN_FAILED and SESSION_PERSIST_FAILED are the retryable cutover-mint failures that leave the source active, aborting before deactivation). Migration state is in-memory only (`AppState.orchestration_state`); an app kill restarts from `prepare_migration`, but the destination sovereign session it persists (via `identity_store` `{did}:oauth-tokens`) survives — a restarted wallet reconstructs the destination client from that record (`sovereign_session::stored_bearer_client`), not from `OutboundMigrationState`. The orchestrator never POSTs plc.directory — the single PLC write is `migrate::submit_migration_op_cmd`
- `src/disaster_recovery.rs` — Sovereign disaster recovery (5 Tauri IPC commands — "Rebuild from backup" on the identity screen): rebuild the account on a new (or the same) PDS from the iCloud backups when the source PDS is gone or uncooperative, the ATProto "adversarial migration" pattern automated by the wallet's custody of `rotationKeys[0]`. `prepare_disaster_recovery(did, dest_pds_url, handle_override?)` (resolve the destination `describeServer` DID + current PLC state from plc.directory alone — the dead source is never contacted; `handle_override` is the fallback for a handle whose domain the dead PDS served; opens a `recovery: true` orchestration session), `enroll_recovery_signing_key(did)` (PLC op #1: generate — or reuse across retries — a self-controlled P-256 `atproto` signing key, persist its scalar to the per-DID `recovery-signing-key` Keychain slot with read-back verify BEFORE any network call, then build + device-key-sign + submit the enroll op directly to plc.directory; reconciles to success if a prior attempt already landed; biometric-gated in the frontend), `await_recovery_key_visibility(did)` (one audit-log poll: is the enrolled key the DID's `atproto` method yet? advances the phase gate when it is — `createAccount` cannot run before op #1 propagates), `create_recovery_destination_account(did, email, invite_code?)` (re-verify visibility, mint the service-auth JWT **offline** with the self-controlled key — `iss` = account DID, `aud` = destination server DID, `lxm` = `com.atproto.server.createAccount`, 1h expiry, via `crypto::mint_service_auth_jwt` — and run the shared migration `createAccount` core; the destination verifies the JWT against plc.directory, so this works against any PDS), and `recovery_transfer_repo(app, did)` (importRepo from the validated iCloud CAR via `repo_backup::mirror_repo_car`; `BACKUP_UNAVAILABLE` when no valid snapshot exists). The transfer tail reuses the orchestrator's shared commands against the same session: `transfer_blobs` (mirror-primary — the drain reads `mirror_fallback_blob` directly, no doomed source fetches), `transfer_preferences` (honest no-op skip: no preferences backup exists), `verify_import`, `arm_identity_leg` + the `migrate.rs` identity leg (PLC op #2: adopt the destination's recommended keys + `services` repoint, wallet device key still at `rotationKeys[0]`), and `finalize_migration` (activate the destination; no source to deactivate). The strict pre-sign guard `guard_recovery_enroll_op` is the FIFTH wallet allowlist and the narrowest: ONLY the `atproto` verification method may change, to exactly the freshly generated key (fresh = not a rotation key, not an existing method) — rotationKeys must be byte-identical with the device key at `[0]` (the anti-lockout rule from the adversarial-migration write-up), alsoKnownAs and services preserved (the `atproto_pds` repoint belongs to op #2). The created account stays deactivated until the final activation, so an abort at any earlier step leaves nothing half-live; a stolen device key attempting this is caught by `plc_monitor` + the 72-hour recovery window. `DisasterRecoveryError` (WALLET_NOT_AUTHORIZED, GUARD_REJECTED, INVALID_AUDIT_LOG, SIGNING_FAILED, KEYCHAIN_ERROR, IDENTITY_NOT_FOUND, PLC_DIRECTORY_ERROR, RATE_LIMITED, KEY_NOT_ENROLLED, DESTINATION_UNREACHABLE, RECOVERY_NOT_READY, NETWORK_ERROR) serialized as `{ code: "SCREAMING_SNAKE_CASE" }` with camelCase fields; the orchestration-half commands return `MigrationError` (whose `BACKUP_UNAVAILABLE` variant is recovery-specific)
- `src/endpoint_repair.rs` — sovereign "repair hosting endpoint" flow for a wallet-custodied did:plc (1 Tauri IPC command, `repair_hosting_endpoint(did, new_endpoint)`): when the hosting server changes hostname underneath the account, the DID document's `atproto_pds` endpoint points at a dead host and every client misroutes — and a passwordless account can only mint the session the server-signed `signPlcOperation` path needs against that same dead host. So the wallet device-key-signs the repoint itself and submits DIRECTLY to plc.directory; the only network dependencies are plc.directory and the NEW endpoint, never the old one. The new endpoint is normalized to a bare https origin (`normalize_endpoint`) and probed via the public `com.atproto.sync.getRepoStatus` to prove it actually hosts this DID before anything signs (`DESTINATION_NOT_HOSTING` otherwise). `guard_endpoint_repair` is the SIXTH strict wallet allowlist and the narrowest service mutation: ONLY the `atproto_pds` endpoint string may change — rotationKeys, verificationMethods, alsoKnownAs, every other service, and even the `atproto_pds` service type must be byte-identical, and a no-op endpoint must reconcile (an already-correct document returns success with `opCid: null`) rather than sign. `EndpointRepairError` (WALLET_NOT_AUTHORIZED, INVALID_ENDPOINT, DESTINATION_UNREACHABLE, DESTINATION_NOT_HOSTING, GUARD_REJECTED, INVALID_AUDIT_LOG, SIGNING_FAILED, PLC_DIRECTORY_ERROR, RATE_LIMITED, NETWORK_ERROR, IDENTITY_NOT_FOUND) serialized as `{ code: "SCREAMING_SNAKE_CASE" }` with camelCase fields; the frontend gates `repairHostingEndpoint` behind `authenticateBiometric()`, and the `EndpointRepairScreen` is reached from DIDDocumentScreen's "Repair hosting endpoint" (root-key did:plc only)
- `src/handle_change.rs` — sovereign "change handle" flow for a wallet-custodied did:plc (MM-305). Two Tauri commands: `get_identity_handle_domains(did)` (discovers the DID's HOSTING PDS via `discover_pds`, returns its `describeServer.availableUserDomains` — distinct from the create flow's `get_available_user_domains`, which targets only the configured Custos) and `change_handle_cmd(did, handle)` — the full passwordless flow: resolve a full-access session (`session_provider::SessionProvider::full_access_client`, MM-353), call `com.atproto.identity.updateHandle` on the hosting PDS (PDS arbitrates served-domain allocation / uniqueness / reserved names), then build + **device-key-sign** the `alsoKnownAs` PLC op via `crypto::build_did_plc_rotation_op`, POST it to plc.directory, and refresh the cached PLC log + DID doc. Ordering is `updateHandle` FIRST, PLC op SECOND (a failure between self-heals on retry: `build_handle_op` re-reads the audit log each attempt, and an op that already landed makes the desired `alsoKnownAs` current → reconciles to success without a re-POST). The strict pre-sign guard `guard_handle_change` is the THIRD wallet allowlist — the mirror image of `migrate::guard_migration_op`: **alsoKnownAs MAY change; rotationKeys, verificationMethods, and services must NOT** (+ device key must be in the current rotationKeys, else `WalletNotAuthorized`). Pure helpers: `guard_handle_change`, `latest_full_state` (full current state incl. VMs + services maps), `compute_new_also_known_as` (new `at://{handle}` primary, prior `at://` handles dropped, non-handle aliases preserved), `classify_update_handle_error`. `HandleChangeError` (WALLET_NOT_AUTHORIZED, SESSION_LOCKED{reason}, RATE_LIMITED, HANDLE_NOT_AVAILABLE, INVALID_HANDLE, UPDATE_HANDLE_FAILED, GUARD_REJECTED, INVALID_AUDIT_LOG, SIGNING_FAILED, PLC_DIRECTORY_ERROR, SERVER_ERROR, NETWORK_ERROR, IDENTITY_NOT_FOUND) — `SESSION_LOCKED` carries the `session_provider::UnlockReason` and is the cue for the frontend to run `sovereignLogin(did)` and retry. A directory read (`fetch_audit_log`/`fetch_plc_data_document`/`discover_pds`) is classified via `map_plc_fetch_error` (throttle → RATE_LIMITED, HTTP verdict → PLC_DIRECTORY_ERROR, transport → NETWORK_ERROR) and a session-lifecycle failure via `map_session_error` (a server verdict/unsupported-host/keychain/malformed-response failure → SERVER_ERROR, never NETWORK_ERROR). The biometric gate is in the frontend (`$lib/ipc/handle-change.ts`'s `changeHandle`), in front of the Secure-Enclave signing
- `src/rotate_repo_key.rs` — sovereign repo signing-key rotation for a wallet-custodied did:plc (ADR-0025): replace the PDS-held commit-signing key (`verificationMethods.atproto` / the PDS `rotationKeys` slot) with a freshly generated one — the recovery move when the PDS key's at-rest encryption is compromised or its master key is lost. Two Tauri commands: `build_repo_key_rotation_cmd(did) -> SignedRotationOp` (resolve a full-access session via `SessionProvider::full_access_client`, `POST /v1/repo-keys/rotation` on the hosting PDS to stage a fresh key, fetch the audit log via `handle_change::latest_full_state`, compose the op — device key stays `rotationKeys[0]`, staged key takes the PDS slot + the `atproto` method, services/alsoKnownAs preserved — run the strict guard, device-key-sign via `crypto::build_did_plc_rotation_op`, park in `AppState.rotation_state`) and `submit_repo_key_rotation_cmd(did) -> ClaimResult` (`POST /v1/repo-keys/rotation/complete` with the parked op — **the wallet never POSTs this op to plc.directory itself**: the PDS submits it and cuts its commit signer over atomically under the account's repo write lock, so no commit is ever signed by a key absent from the DID doc — then refresh the cached PLC log + DID doc; the PDS side is retry-safe, so the op stays parked until success). `guard_rotation_op` is the FOURTH strict wallet allowlist: **the atproto verification method and the PDS rotationKeys slot move to exactly the PDS-staged key; rotationKeys must be exactly `[device, staged]`, other verificationMethods entries, services, and alsoKnownAs must NOT change** (+ device key must be in the current rotationKeys, else `WalletNotAuthorized`; a staged key already present in the doc is rejected as non-fresh). Pure helpers: `guard_rotation_op`, `build_rotation_diff`. `RotationError` (WALLET_NOT_AUTHORIZED, SESSION_LOCKED{reason}, RATE_LIMITED, GUARD_REJECTED, INVALID_AUDIT_LOG, SIGNING_FAILED, ROTATION_FAILED{status}, PLC_DIRECTORY_ERROR, SERVER_ERROR, NETWORK_ERROR, IDENTITY_NOT_FOUND, NO_PENDING_ROTATION) — directory reads classify via `map_plc_fetch_error` and session-lifecycle failures via `map_session_error`, the same split as `HandleChangeError`. The biometric gate is in the frontend (`$lib/ipc/rotation.ts`'s `submitRepoKeyRotation`), in front of the irreversible submission
- `src/lib.rs::check_identity_status() -> Result<Vec<IdentityStatus>, MonitorError>` — Tauri IPC command (delegates to `PlcMonitor::check_all`)
- `src/lib.rs::list_identities() -> Result<Vec<String>, IdentityStoreError>` — Tauri IPC command: returns managed DIDs from Keychain via `IdentityStore::list_identities()`; returns empty list if no identities claimed
- `src/lib.rs::get_stored_did_doc(did: String) -> Result<Option<serde_json::Value>, IdentityStoreError>` — Tauri IPC command: retrieves stored DID document as parsed JSON for a claimed identity; returns None if not stored
- `src/lib.rs::get_device_key_id(did: String) -> Result<String, IdentityStoreError>` — Tauri IPC command: returns the device key's did:key URI for a claimed identity via `IdentityStore::get_or_create_device_key()`
- `src/sovereign_session.rs::sovereign_login(did: String) -> Result<SovereignLoginResult, SovereignLoginError>` — Tauri IPC command: mints and persists a full-access Bearer session with the selected DID's current rotation key; frontend callers use `sovereignLogin(did)`, which gates the IPC call behind `authenticateBiometric()` so cancellation signs and sends nothing
- `src/session_provider.rs::ensure_identity_session(did: String) -> Result<SessionReady, SessionError>` — Tauri IPC command: the frontend pre-flight. Restores or rotates the DID's session and reports status (dropping the in-Rust client); a `NEEDS_UNLOCK` error is the cue for the UI to offer the passwordless `sovereignLogin(did)`. Performs **no** biometric prompt — a live token must never demand one. Frontend wrapper: `ensureIdentitySession(did)`.
- `src/lib.rs::register_created_identity(did: String, handle: String) -> Result<(), RegisterIdentityError>` — Tauri IPC command: registers a just-created identity in `IdentityStore` so it appears in `IdentityListHome` (the create flow otherwise writes only the OAuth session + legacy `"did"` Keychain item, which the home screen does not read). Calls `add_identity` (tolerating `IdentityAlreadyExists`), `adopt_global_device_key` (so the per-DID key matches the genesis rotation key), and stores a locally-built PLC-format DID document (handle + PDS + rotationKeys). Mirrors `claim::submit_claim`'s persistence step. `RegisterIdentityError` { KEYCHAIN_ERROR } serialized as `{ code: "SCREAMING_SNAKE_CASE" }`
- `src/lib.rs::get_pds_url() -> Option<String>` — Tauri IPC command: loads PDS base URL from Keychain, returns Some(url) if configured or None for first-launch
- `src/lib.rs::save_pds_url(url: String) -> Result<(), PdsConfigError>` — Tauri IPC command: validates URL format, pings `/xrpc/_health` on the PDS, saves to Keychain, initializes `AppState.custos_client` (runtime configuration), then re-probes the host's advertised capabilities into `pds_capabilities`'s per-host cache (best-effort — the user has just deliberately re-pointed the wallet, which is exactly when a stale verdict would be wrong)
- `src/lib.rs::get_pds_capabilities(pds_url: Option<String>) -> Result<ServerCapabilities, PdsConfigError>` — Tauri IPC command: what the configured PDS (or a named one) advertises, so a screen offers only host-supported features. Cached per host; **an absent `custos` extension and an unreachable host both report an empty list** rather than erroring, so a gate degrades to standard-lexicon behavior instead of failing. Rejects only for a malformed URL
- `src/lib.rs::get_appearance_preference() -> Option<String>` — Tauri IPC command: returns the saved appearance preference (`"system"` | `"light"` | `"dark"`) from the Keychain, or None if never set; a corrupt/unrecognized stored value reads as None (follow the system), never an error
- `src/lib.rs::set_appearance_preference(preference: String) -> Result<(), AppearanceError>` — Tauri IPC command: validates the value against the three-value allowlist and persists it to the Keychain. `AppearanceError` { INVALID_PREFERENCE, KEYCHAIN_ERROR } serialized as `{ code: "SCREAMING_SNAKE_CASE" }`

**Guarantees:**
- `crate-type = ["staticlib", "cdylib", "rlib"]` supports iOS (staticlib), Android (cdylib), and normal cargo builds (rlib)
- `src/main.rs` is the desktop entry point; `src/lib.rs::run()` is the iOS/Android entry point (via `#[cfg_attr(mobile, tauri::mobile_entry_point)]`)
- `tauri.conf.json` configures the bundle identifier, dev URL (`http://localhost:5173`), and frontend dist path (`../dist`)
- `create_account` maps PDS HTTP error codes to typed `CreateAccountError` variants (EXPIRED_CODE, REDEEMED_CODE, EMAIL_TAKEN, HANDLE_TAKEN, NETWORK_ERROR, UNKNOWN) serialized as `{ code: "SCREAMING_SNAKE" }` for the frontend
- `perform_did_ceremony` maps failures to typed `DIDCeremonyError` variants (KEY_NOT_FOUND, PDS_KEY_FETCH_FAILED, NO_PDS_SIGNING_KEY, SHARE_GENERATION_FAILED, SIGNING_FAILED, DID_CREATION_FAILED, KEYCHAIN_ERROR, SHARE_STORAGE_FAILED, NETWORK_ERROR) serialized as `{ code: "SCREAMING_SNAKE_CASE" }` for the frontend; `confirm_share_backup` maps to `ShareBackupError` (SHARE_NOT_STORED, KEYCHAIN_ERROR)
- `prepare_oauth_flow` / `complete_oauth_flow` map failures to typed `OAuthError` variants (DPOP_KEY_GEN_FAILED, DPOP_KEY_INVALID, DPOP_PROOF_FAILED, KEYCHAIN_ERROR, STATE_MISMATCH, CALLBACK_ABANDONED, PAR_FAILED, TOKEN_EXCHANGE_FAILED, TOKEN_REFRESH_FAILED, INVALID_GRANT, NOT_AUTHENTICATED) serialized as `{ code: "SCREAMING_SNAKE_CASE" }` for the frontend
- The OAuth callback is delivered by **`ASWebAuthenticationSession`** (via the vendored `tauri-plugin-auth-session`), **not** a deep link. The frontend calls `prepare_*` (Rust) for the authorize URL, then `plugin:auth-session|start` (which opens the in-app auth sheet and returns the `org.obsign.identitywallet:/oauth/callback?code=...&state=...` URL), then `complete_*` (Rust) to finish. The custom scheme `org.obsign.identitywallet` is registered in `src-tauri/Info.ios.plist` (`CFBundleURLTypes`, alongside the legacy `dev.malpercio.identitywallet` transition entry) because it is the session's `callbackURLScheme`. **Why not deep links:** iOS Safari will not auto-launch the app from a server-side redirect to a custom scheme, so the old `tauri-plugin-deep-link` + `on_open_url` + `handle_deep_link` flow silently failed; ASWebAuthenticationSession captures the callback itself
- On app startup, if OAuth tokens exist in Keychain, the session is restored into `AppState.oauth_session` and an `auth_ready` Tauri event is emitted after a 300ms delay (allows SvelteKit to boot and register its listener)
- `OAuthClient` transparently refreshes access tokens with <60s remaining before each request; retries once on `use_dpop_nonce` 400 responses from the server.
