I'm thinking through the design changes needed here. The main decision is making `RemovalOutcome.tombstone_cid` optional—using `Option<String>` on the Rust side with `#[serde(skip_serializing_if)]` to avoid serializing null values, and on the TypeScript side it becomes `tombstoneCid: string | null`. Since the frontend doesn't actually use this field anywhere, making it optional is straightforward.

For the backend flow with did:web identities, the tricky part is handling the window between `deleteAccount` succeeding and the local wipe failing. The key insight is to keep the pending marker as a genuine signal that account deletion is in progress with local cleanup still needed, but make the tombstone operation method-aware—for did:web, skip the tombstone step entirely and only do the local wipe, which prevents the reconciliation from getting wedged since `tombstone_identity` would also branch on the method and handle did:web as wipe-only.

So I'm introducing a shared function that returns either `None` for did:web (wipe-only, no tombstone cid) or `Some(cid)` for other methods (full tombstone path). This guards against the wedge even if someone calls the raw command directly. The UI also needs to hide the "retire on network" checkbox for did:web identities since that operation would now be a lie—it'd silently do a local wipe while claiming network retirement.

For the UI ungating, I need to be careful: the ticket says drop the did:plc condition on `onremove`, but I should only allow did:plc or did:web explicitly rather than opening it to unknown DID methods, since anything else would hit the plc.directory path and fail.

The cleanest approach is a small helper that maps each DID method to its removal strategy — did:plc gets a tombstone, did:web gets local-only deletion, and anything else... well, the wallet's IdentityStore only manages those two anyway, so I can handle unknowns defensively.

I'm writing a helper function that checks if a DID is a did:plc (the only method with a PLC log to tombstone), then branching the removal logic on that. For the UI copy, I'll check explicitly for did:web to show the epilogue about did.json, and fall back to generic text otherwise.

Now I need to check what copy the did:web ceremony's publish step uses for consistency, and verify that `request_identity_removal` works for did:web by confirming the session was persisted during migration or the ceremony and that `discover_pds` can find the PDS.

But there's a problem: did:web has no rotation keys, so if the session record is lost, `sovereignLogin` can't re-mint a sovereign session — the finalize_migration comment explicitly says this is impossible for did:web. 107	/// Fetch the DID document to serve for a Custos-hosted `did:web` account, gated on the opt-in.
108	///
109	/// Returns `Some(document)` only when the account for `did` exists, has managed did:web hosting
110	/// enabled (`did_web_hosting_enabled_at IS NOT NULL`), is in an active lifecycle (not deactivated,
111	/// suspended, or taken down — the same all-NULL gate as every other serving path), and has a stored
112	/// document. Any of those failing yields `None`, so the `.well-known/did.json` route 404s a host
113	/// that isn't opted in exactly as it does an unknown one — no existence oracle for the opt-in state.
114	///
115	/// The caller is responsible for having mapped the request host to `did:web:{host}`; this query does
116	/// not itself constrain the DID method, but a `did:plc` account never sets the opt-in column, so it
117	/// can never be served here.
118	pub async fn serve_hosted_did_document(
119	    db: &SqlitePool,
120	    did: &str,
121	) -> Result<Option<serde_json::Value>, ApiError> {
122	    let row: Option<(String,)> = sqlx::query_as(
123	        "SELECT d.document \
124	         FROM accounts a \
125	         JOIN did_documents d ON d.did = a.did \
126	         WHERE a.did = ? \
127	           AND a.did_web_hosting_enabled_at IS NOT NULL \
128	           AND a.deactivated_at IS NULL \
129	           AND a.suspended_at IS NULL \
130	           AND a.taken_down_at IS NULL \
131	         LIMIT 1",
132	    )
133	    .bind(did)
134	    .fetch_optional(db)
135	    .await
136	    .map_err(|e| {
137	        tracing::error!(did = %did, error = %e, "DB error fetching hosted DID document");
138	        ApiError::new(ErrorCode::InternalError, "failed to load DID document")
139	    })?;
140	
141	    match row {
142	        None => Ok(None),
143	        Some((doc_str,)) => {
144	            let doc = serde_json::from_str(&doc_str).map_err(|e| {
145	                let preview = &doc_str[..doc_str.len().min(500)];
146	                tracing::error!(did = %did, error = %e, raw = %preview, "malformed hosted DID document in DB");
147	                ApiError::new(ErrorCode::InternalError, "malformed DID document")
148	            })?;
149	            Ok(Some(doc))
150	        }
151	    }
152	}

# PDS Crate (Custos)

Last verified: 2026-07-13

## Purpose

The PDS is the axum-based web server. It is the sole Imperative Shell in the workspace —
the only crate that touches SQLite, handles HTTP, or manages process-level state. All other
crates (`crypto`, `repo-engine`, `common`) are pure Functional Cores that the PDS calls.

## Module Map

```
src/
  main.rs          — startup: open pool, run migrations, bind server
  telemetry.rs     — OTel tracing-subscriber init (`init_subscriber`) + shutdown-flushing `OtelGuard`; wired by main.rs at startup, dropped after graceful shutdown. `[telemetry] log_format = "json"` switches the stdout fmt layer to one-JSON-object-per-line
  metrics.rs       — OTel meter + Prometheus registry behind `GET /metrics` (see "Metrics" section below): typed `Metrics` handle in AppState, instrument/label name constants (`metrics::names`), the `http_requests_total` middleware, and the `SubscriberGuard` RAII gauge
  app.rs           — router construction (route table + shared middleware layers); re-exports `AppState`/`FailedLoginStore` (and, under `#[cfg(test)]`, `test_state`/`test_state_with_plc_url`) from `state.rs` so the ~120 existing `crate::app::AppState` imports across the crate stay unchanged
  state.rs         — `AppState` definition + `FailedLoginStore`, plus the `#[cfg(test)]` `test_state`/`test_state_with_plc_url` constructors
  xrpc_dispatch.rs — the catch-all XRPC proxy dispatcher (`xrpc_handler`, registered by `app.rs` at `/xrpc/{method}`): resolves `app.bsky.*`/`chat.bsky.*`/`com.atproto.moderation.*` to an upstream (configured default or an `atproto-proxy`-header target), enforces the read-after-write munge branch, and records `proxy_requests_total`
  firehose/        — persistent subscribeRepos event pipeline (durable sequencer + broadcast fan-out)
  firehose_gc.rs   — periodic `repo_seq` retention sweep (age/count pruning below the live frontier)
  blob_store.rs    — blob storage backend: filesystem I/O, CID computation, MIME-type detection; blobs live at `{data_dir}/blobs/{cid[0:2]}/{cid}`
  blob_gc.rs       — periodic blob GC over per-account ownership rows (`blob_owners`, V039): reconciles each account's MST-referenced blobs into its ownership rows (permanent vs released-with-grace, adopting referenced-but-unowned stored CIDs), then sweeps expired unreferenced rows — the shared physical row + file are deleted only when the last owner is gone
  blob_mirror/     — off-volume blob replication to an S3-compatible bucket (`[blob_mirror]` / `EZPDS_BLOB_MIRROR_*`, the Litestream analogue for blob files, which Litestream never covers): `mod.rs` is the periodic sweep (template: blob_gc.rs — upload verified-missing keys, propagate row deletions on a harmless lag, with a tripwire refusing delete propagation when the `blobs` table is empty against a non-empty bucket) plus `restore_missing_blobs`, run by main.rs *before the listener binds* so a Litestream-restored DB is reconciled with the blob directory before anything is served; `s3.rs` is a minimal hand-rolled SigV4 client (put/get/delete/ListObjectsV2, signing pinned against the AWS documentation's worked examples). Both mirror directions re-hash bytes against their CID (`blob_store::compute_cid`) before trusting them: a corrupt local file never becomes the recovery copy, and a corrupt bucket copy is never materialised at a valid CID path. `BlobMirror::fetch_verified` (fetch + verify one CID) is the shared entry point `blob_scrub.rs`'s auto-heal reuses. `test_support.rs` (`#[cfg(test)]`) holds the shared fake-S3 test double + `BlobMirror` builder both this module's and `blob_scrub.rs`'s tests use
  blob_scrub.rs    — periodic blob-integrity scrub sweep (`[blob_scrub]` / `EZPDS_BLOB_SCRUB_*`, template: blob_gc.rs, same failed-pass-leaves-timestamp-stale posture): re-hashes every stored blob's file against its `blobs` row (hash + size) and walks the blob directory for both orphan directions nothing else scans for — a row whose file is missing (the migration-blocking fault) and a file no row owns (a leak `blob_gc` never sees, since it only ever works from DB rows outward). When `[blob_mirror]` is configured and `auto_heal` is on, a bad/missing file is repaired from the bucket's verified copy (`BlobMirror::fetch_verified`, written back through `blob_store::store_blob`'s durable temp-file+fsync+rename path so a healed file is exactly as crash-durable as a fresh upload); otherwise the problem is only ever flagged, converting silent rot into an operator signal
```

### `firehose/`

The **persistent** event pipeline behind `com.atproto.sync.subscribeRepos`, split into three
cohesive layers so the subtle invariant-heavy staging code is reviewable in isolation. `mod.rs`
re-exports every submodule's public types (`Firehose`, `FirehoseEvent`, `CommitInput`, `Subscription`,
etc.) at `crate::firehose::*`, so the 19 consumer files address them exactly as before the split.

| File | Contents |
|---|---|
| `mod.rs` | `Firehose` (the durable sequencer + broadcast fan-out), the bare `emit_commit`/`emit_account`/`emit_identity`/`emit_sync` primitives, and the atomic staged-transaction path (`lock_emit`/`EmitGuard`/`PendingCommit`/`PendingAccount`/`PendingWithSync`) — the emit-lock/staging invariants documented below |
| `events.rs` | The wire-facing event model (`RepoOp`, `CommitEvent`, `AccountEvent`, `IdentityEvent`, `SyncEvent`, `FirehoseEvent`), their DAG-CBOR stored-payload encoding, `decode_stored_event` (reconstructs an event from a persisted `repo_seq` row for replay), and the pre-persist wire-CID/CAR-size validation. Pure data + (de)serialization, no `Firehose` state |
| `replay.rs` | Cursor replay over the durable log: `Subscription`/`SubscribeOutcome` (the subscribe handshake) and `ReplayReader` (paged `(cursor, upper]` replay with the best-effort-vs-fail-closed pruning logic) |

The module holds a durable
monotonic sequencer (backed by the `repo_seq` table, V028) and a Tokio `broadcast` channel;
`AppState.firehose: Arc<Firehose>` is shared by every handler. Each repo commit calls
`record_write::commit_repo_write`, which builds the commit's block diff
(`repo_engine::collect_commit_diff` — one walk of the new root, yielding both the `added` diff
blocks and the `new_reachable` keep-set — + `build_car_from_cids`, run *before* post-commit GC) and
publishes a sequenced `CommitEvent` carrying the DID, rev, `since`, `prevData` (the previous
commit's MST root CID — Sync v1.1's inductive-validation anchor, captured before the write mutates
the repo; `None` for genesis), per-record `RepoOp`s (action + collection/rkey + cid + prev + value;
`prev` is the previous record CID for an update/delete — Sync v1.1's per-op inductive-validation
anchor — `None` for a create), and
the CARv1 diff blocks. The `#commit` wire frame emits the deprecated `blobs` list empty. Backpressure is by design: the bounded
channel never blocks producers — a slow subscriber observes `Lagged` and is expected to disconnect.
All three write paths (`create_record`/`put_record` via `record_write`, `delete_record`,
`apply_writes`) emit exactly one event per commit. (Those same write paths reject a deactivated
account with 403 before committing.) `create_did.rs`'s `promote_account` stages the same kind of
`#commit` event for a new account's *genesis* repo, atomically with the `accounts`/`did_documents`/
`sessions` inserts, so a fresh host self-announces to the relay instead of staying invisible until
its first record write; chained after that genesis `#commit` in the same transaction is a Sync v1.1
`#sync` state assertion (via `PendingCommit::stage_sync`, carrying a single-root CAR of just the
signed commit block), so a relay can anchor to this fresh host's head. It then emits a best-effort
`#account` (active) frame and calls `crawlers.notify()` once that transaction has committed.
A `#sync` frame (`SyncEvent`: DID, rev, and a ≤10 KB commit-block CAR) is the Sync v1.1 head
assertion relays use to auto-repair drift; it is emitted on account genesis (above) and on
`activateAccount` (chained after the `#account` via `PendingAccount::stage_sync` when the account
has a repo — the commit-block CAR is built *before* the transaction, since the single-connection
pool can't serve a block read while the tx holds the connection). `importRepo` (shipped,
`routes/import_repo.rs`) deliberately does *not* emit one — a migrated repo's head assertion rides
on the `activateAccount` that follows it in the migration sequence. Account-status changes emit a separate
`#account` frame instead of a `#commit`: `activate_account.rs`/`deactivate_account.rs` stage one
via `Firehose::stage_account` (active=false/`deactivated` or active=true) **only on a real status
transition** — a redundant no-op activate/deactivate returns 200 and emits nothing.
`update_subject_status.rs` (`com.atproto.admin.updateSubjectStatus`) stages the same kind of frame
for an admin-driven takedown/clear, but derives `active`/`status` from the account's full
`AccountLifecycle` after the write rather than assuming its own dimension won — clearing a
takedown on a still-suspended account must report `suspended`, not `active`. The `#account` frame
shares the same sequencer so account frames are ordered relative to commits.

**Durability and atomicity.** `Firehose::emit_commit`/`emit_account`/`emit_identity`/`emit_sync`
persist each event to
`repo_seq` (via `db::firehose_seq`) **before** broadcasting it, all under one async `emit_lock`
that keeps broadcast order = `seq` order and the log a dense prefix (a failed insert doesn't
consume a `seq`). The sequencer loads `MAX(seq)` on construction, so `seq` is monotonic across
restarts/redeploys. Those methods remain bare best-effort primitives — used directly by tests,
`emit_identity`'s neighbours (`create_handle.rs`/`delete_handle.rs`/`update_handle.rs`), and
`create_did.rs`'s post-commit `emit_account` call, none of which need atomicity with a specific
transaction; the call sites that do instead acquire `emit_lock` via `Firehose::lock_emit`
(returning an `EmitGuard`) *before* opening their transaction, then call
`EmitGuard::stage_commit`/`stage_account` to insert the `repo_seq` row into that *caller's own*
open transaction. A caller that also needs a chained `#sync` in the same transaction (genesis,
activation) calls `PendingCommit::stage_sync`/`PendingAccount::stage_sync`, which inserts the
`#sync` row at the next `seq` and returns a `PendingWithSync` whose `finish` broadcasts the primary
event then the `#sync`, advancing the counter past both. The staging insert lands in the caller's
open transaction — the same one carrying the repo-root CAS (`record_write::commit_repo_write`,
`create_did.rs`'s genesis promotion) or the account-status UPDATE (`activate_account`/
`deactivate_account`) — and get back a `Pending*` handle that carries the guard forward. Acquiring
the lock before the transaction (rather than inside the staging call) matters on this crate's
single-connection pool: `emit_commit`/
`emit_account`/`emit_identity` already acquire the lock before touching the pool, so a staging
path that instead opened its transaction first and acquired the lock after could deadlock against
one of them (each would hold what the other is waiting for). The caller commits that transaction
and only then calls `Pending*::finish` to advance `last_seq` and broadcast; a failed insert rolls
the whole transaction back (via `?`/`Drop`) rather than landing the state change with a
silently-dropped event, and dropping a `Pending*` without finishing never advances the sequence,
so the seq is retried by the next emit. The one asymmetric drop — a handler future cancelled
(client disconnect) *after* its `tx.commit()` made the staged row durable but before `finish` —
leaves `last_seq` behind the durable log; every insert goes through
`Firehose::insert_at_frontier`, which detects the resulting PRIMARY KEY collision, re-derives the
frontier from the durable `MAX(seq)`, and retries once, so one cancelled request costs one
never-broadcast event (still replayable from the log, like any pre-restart event) instead of
wedging all writes until restart. `subscribe_from(cursor)` snapshots the live receiver and
the sequence frontier `upper` together under
`emit_lock`; the `sync_subscribe_repos` handler then pages the durable log for `(cursor, upper]`
(`events_in_range`, decoded via `decode_stored_event`) and streams live events (`seq > upper`)
after — the two ranges are exactly disjoint, so the replay→live boundary has no gap and no
duplication, and replay now survives a restart (it reads the log, not an in-memory buffer). The
subscriber-facing WebSocket frame encoding lives in the `sync_subscribe_repos` handler.

### `crawler.rs`

Outbound `com.atproto.sync.requestCrawl` notifier. `AppState.crawlers: Arc<CrawlerNotifier>`
is shared by every handler. The re-invitation fires from three places: **(1)** on startup
(`main.rs` calls `crawlers.notify()` once when crawlers are configured — a fresh deploy is exactly
when a dropped relay subscription must be re-invited); **(2)** on **every firehose emission**, via
`Firehose::broadcast` (the single fan-out choke point), which the notifier is attached to at boot
(`attach_crawlers`) — so `#commit` **and** the `#account`/`#identity`/`#sync` lifecycle frames all
re-invite the relay, not just repo commits; **(3)** the same broadcast path covers `create_did.rs`/
`create_account_xrpc.rs`/`agent_child.rs`, which additionally call `notify()` directly after their
own commit path. `notify` is fire-and-forget: it selects the crawlers outside their rate-limit
window (one notification per crawler per 30s), then spawns a detached task per crawler that POSTs
`{ "hostname": <PDS-host> }` to `<url>/xrpc/com.atproto.sync.requestCrawl`, retrying with
exponential backoff up to 3 times. All outcomes are logged, never propagated — an emission never
blocks on or fails because of a crawler. Configured via `[crawlers] urls = [...]` (default
`["https://bsky.network"]`; empty disables) or `EZPDS_CRAWLERS`.

Why notify on non-commit frames matters: a relay can silently drop its subscription to a quiet
PDS, and if the PDS only re-invited on commits, a post-migration `#account`(active)/`#sync` burst
emitted while nobody was listening would leave the network's last word on the DID as the source
PDS's deactivation — the DID stuck `AccountDeactivated` network-wide until a repo write happens to
fire another `requestCrawl`. Emitting on the lifecycle frames closes that gap; the durable
`repo_seq` log means the relay's replay heals everything once it reconnects (within retention).

### `relay_status.rs`

The **inbound** half of federation health, complementing `crawler.rs`'s outbound `requestCrawl`:
a `com.atproto.sync.getHostStatus` client that asks the configured relay what it knows about this
PDS. Backs `GET /v1/admin/relay-status` (route `admin_relay_status.rs`), the operator's "is my
server actually federating right now" readout. `fetch_host_status` returns a `RelayReport`:
`Found(HostStatus{ seq, account_count, status })` (the relay's cursor into *our* firehose seq-space,
how many of our accounts it has indexed, and the lifecycle status it assigns us), `NotFound` (the
relay is up but has never crawled us — a normal "not federating yet" state, distinct from an
outage), or `Unreachable(reason)` (transport failure, timeout, non-2xx, or unparseable body). It is
**total, never fatal** — every failure path becomes a variant rather than an `Err`, so the admin
readout always renders the literal truth of what the relay said.

The gap the readout reports is `pdsHeadSeq − relaySeq`, and `pdsHeadSeq` is our **exact** sequencer
head (`firehose.current_seq()`): because we own the PDS, the route reads the head directly instead
of the timed-`subscribeRepos` approximation a third-party observer must make. This module only
fetches the relay's side; `admin_relay_status.rs` does the compare. Like `admin_health.rs`, the
route reports raw truth only — the ok/warn/behind verdict (gap thresholds, status mapping) lives
with the operator (the companion app's relay-status block), never in the API shape. The `#[serde]`
status string is kept verbatim (not an enum) so an unknown value from a newer relay is passed
through rather than dropped. `POST /v1/admin/request-crawl` (route `admin_request_crawl.rs`) is the
companion action: the operator "Request crawl" button, driving `CrawlerNotifier::request_crawl_now`
to re-invite every configured relay immediately (bypassing the 30s auto-notify window) and reporting
each relay's outcome.

### `rate_limit.rs`

Reference-parity request rate limiting. The pure sliding-window algorithm (`MultiWindowLimiter`,
supporting several windows per key with weighted "points") lives in `auth/rate_limit.rs` (Functional
Core); this module is the Imperative Shell that owns the process-level `Mutex`-wrapped limiters and
the Axum middleware. Three families, all off when `[rate_limit] enabled = false` (the test harness
sets this):

1. **Global per-IP** — 1 point/request keyed by client IP (leftmost `X-Forwarded-For`, else the TCP
   peer), default 3000/5min. `com.atproto.sync.getRepo`, `subscribeRepos`, and `_health` are exempt
   so relay backfill/firehose and platform health checks are never throttled.
2. **Per-endpoint per-IP** — tighter caps on `createAccount`/`createSession` (password and
   sovereign session creation share one budget)/`resetPassword`/
   `updateHandle` (plus the native `/v1/accounts[/mobile]` signup routes), `/v1/transfer/accept`
   (authenticated by a bare 6-char code, so a short-code endpoint belongs here by default), and
   the agent claim-ceremony pair `/agent/identity/claim/confirm` + `/v1/agents/claim-preview`
   (both validate a guessable 6-digit `user_code`; they **share one limiter instance** so
   alternating endpoints can't double the guess budget), and the escrow-recovery pair
   `/v1/recovery/initiate` + `/v1/recovery/release` (the release endpoint validates an emailed
   OTP; both **share one limiter instance** so alternating can't double the OTP-guess budget),
   keyed by IP.
3. **Per-account write points** — create=3/update=2/delete=1 over an hourly + daily window, charged
   in `record_write::commit_repo_write` (the single choke point for all four repo-write routes),
   keyed by the **authenticated** DID. Keying on the verified DID — not an unverified token subject —
   is deliberate: otherwise anyone could drain a victim's budget.

Rejections return `429` with the standard error envelope plus `RateLimit-Limit`/`-Remaining`/
`-Reset` and `Retry-After`; successful requests carry the `RateLimit-*` headers of the tightest
applicable limiter. All knobs are configurable via `[rate_limit]` in `pds.toml` / `EZPDS_RATE_LIMIT_*`
(a knob of `0` disables that specific limiter).

### `iroh_tunnel.rs`

The Iroh QUIC tunnel — a NAT-traversing endpoint devices dial by node id instead of by a
routable address. Opt-in via `[iroh] enabled` (default off); when enabled, `main.rs` loads the
persistent node identity (`auth::load_or_create_iroh_secret_key`, backed by the `iroh_identity`
table so the node id is stable across restarts), binds the endpoint with the `N0` preset (n0
discovery + relays), and spawns a detached accept loop. `[iroh] ipv6` (default true;
`EZPDS_IROH_IPV6`) gates the IPv6 QUIC socket: on a v4-only host (e.g. a Railway container with
no public v6 egress) set it false, and `start` clears the pre-configured IP transports and
re-binds IPv4 only — without it iroh's v6 relay probes fail `NetworkUnreachable` forever, one
WARN every ~80s that buries real errors. `AppState.iroh: Option<Arc<IrohState>>`
holds the bound endpoint and its node-id string; `get_device_pds` advertises that node id.
The accept loop speaks a minimal v0.1 echo protocol on the `ezpds/iroh/0` ALPN — enough to
prove the bidirectional channel and serve as a liveness probe; the real repo-sync / push
protocols register here later. Errors are logged, never propagated (one bad peer never stops
the loop). The endpoint is closed on graceful shutdown, which ends the accept loop.

### `read_after_write/`

**Read-after-write:** Buffered munge path for six munged AppView NSIDs
(`app.bsky.feed.getTimeline`, `getAuthorFeed`, `getPostThread`, `getActorLikes`,
`app.bsky.actor.getProfile`, `getProfiles`). Merges the requester's unindexed records
(fetched from the firehose event log via `get_records_since_rev`) into the AppView's indexed
response. Selects records by comparing the AppView's `atproto-repo-rev` header to the account's
current repo CID (`repo_seq`): records with `indexed_at` timestamps *after* the AppView's rev
are included. The core `pipethrough_munged` handler implements the full fallback ladder:
(1) upstream error → return error unchanged; (2) non-2xx → return buffered original (except
`getPostThread` 400 NotFound, which triggers reconstruction); (3) JSON parse error → return buffered
original; (4) empty LocalRecords → return buffered original with NO lag header; (5) munge/hydration
errors → log and return buffered original (fallback to untouched upstream response). Response buffering
is capped at 10 MiB; oversized responses trigger early bailout. The `Atproto-Upstream-Lag` header
(milliseconds since the oldest merged record's indexed_at) is set only when local.count > 0.
Submodules:

| File | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `mod.rs` | `pipethrough_munged` handler, fallback ladder, buffering cap, response error handling, lag header calculation |
| `munge.rs` | Per-NSID munges `get_timeline`, `get_author_feed`, `get_post_thread`, `get_actor_likes`, `get_profile`, `get_profiles` — injection/overwriting of the requester's records. `// pattern: Mixed (unavoidable)` (the feed/thread munges orchestrate async hydration through `LocalViewer`) |
| `viewer.rs` | `LocalViewer`: hydrates local records as feed items / profile views with author/counts populated via AppView prefetch, renders quote embeds with appview-fetched URIs (falls back to `#viewNotFound` on errors) |
| `types.rs` | `LocalRecords`, `RecordDescript` — structured container for unindexed records bucket by collection |

The munge path shares `service_proxy::proxy_request` extraction with the streaming fast path
(both mint service auth, both buffer request bodies up to MAX_PROXY_BODY, both forward query params).
`mint_service_auth` is `pub(crate)` so `pipethrough_munged` can re-use the JWT minting logic.

**Config:** The AppView is configured via `[appview]` in `pds.toml` (`EZPDS_APPVIEW_URL` env var,
default `https://api.bsky.app`) and `EZPDS_APPVIEW_DID` (default `did:web:api.bsky.app#bsky_appview`).
The optional `EZPDS_APPVIEW_CDN_URL` (default `https://cdn.bsky.app`) overrides the blob CDN
endpoint in blob embed URLs (useful for egress-heavy testing with a local blobstore).

See [`src/db/AGENTS.md`](src/db/AGENTS.md) for migration history and invariants.

**Rule:** `db/` submodules never import from `routes/` or `auth/`. They accept `&SqlitePool`
and return data; callers decide what to do with it.

### `routes/`

One file per HTTP endpoint. Each handler is a thin Imperative Shell:
**gather** (extract state/body/headers) → **process** (call `auth/` or `db/`) → **respond**.

| File | Endpoint |
|---|---|
| `oauth_authorize.rs` | `GET/POST /oauth/authorize` |
| `oauth_par.rs` | `POST /oauth/par` — for discoverable (https URL) client_ids, a private-use-scheme redirect_uri must be the client_id host's reverse-FQDN (`invalid_redirect_uri` otherwise), matching bsky.social's enforcement of the atproto OAuth rule |
| `oauth_token/` | `POST /oauth/token` — one route module split across per-grant submodules: `mod.rs` (request/response types, the shared token-issuance + `cleanup_expired_state` helpers, and the `post_token` grant dispatcher) plus `authorization_code.rs`, `refresh.rs`, `jwt_bearer.rs`, and `claim_polling.rs` (each grant's distinct logic + error surface, and its tests). Still a single route module, so the no-routes-importing-routes rule is untouched. Grants: `authorization_code` + `refresh_token` (DPoP-bound, rotating refresh tokens), `urn:ietf:params:oauth:grant-type:jwt-bearer` (RFC 7523), and `urn:workos:agent-auth:grant-type:claim` (auth.md Step 4c). **jwt-bearer** exchanges a service-signed agent `identity_assertion` for a short-lived **Bearer** access token (no DPoP, no refresh token; the agent identity must be `claimed` with a DID matching the assertion `sub` — unclaimed/absent → `invalid_grant`, `revoked` → `access_denied`, non-origin `resource` → `invalid_target`). The issued token carries the assertion's granular `scope` verbatim (no widening: the grant accepts no requested `scope`) **and** its `registration_id` claim, which marks the token agent-derived (see `auth/extractors.rs::AuthenticatedUser::{is_agent,require_not_agent}`) and ties it to the `agent_identities` row for revocation/audit. **Revocation is bounded by the access-token TTL:** flipping an identity to `revoked` blocks the *next* exchange immediately, but an already-issued access token stays valid until it expires (5 min); there is no live-token revocation list. **claim-polling** is the machine-pollable half of the claim ceremony: a `service_auth`/`anonymous` agent polls with its one-time `claim_token` (no DPoP — it may hold no key yet; the token is the credential) while the owner confirms out-of-band. Reads the identity's lifecycle state and reports it as OAuth device-flow codes — `authorization_pending` (active, ceremony still pending), `expired_token` (`claim_token`/`user_code` window lapsed), `access_denied` (`revoked`), or **200** with a fresh Bearer token + the stored post-claim `identity_assertion` (+ `assertion_expires`) once `claimed` (scope derived from the row's stored scopes, so it matches a jwt-bearer exchange of the same assertion byte-for-byte). Polling faster than the advertised `interval` (`auth/agent_assertion.rs::POLL_INTERVAL_SECS`, 5s) → `slow_down`, throttled by the in-memory `AppState.poll_tracker` keyed by the `claim_token`'s SHA-256 (never the raw secret; pruned in `cleanup_expired_state`) |

Auth is DPoP proof-of-possession like the `refresh_token` grant: the proof's key thumbprint must match the token's bound `jkt` (and, when the caller names a `client_id`, its owning client), so a party that only observed the token string can't revoke it — closing the RFC 7009 DoS-oracle concern. Every well-formed, DPoP-authenticated request returns **200 with an empty body** regardless of whether a token matched (RFC 7009 §2.2 non-disclosure); only a missing `token` (`invalid_request`) or a missing/invalid DPoP proof (`invalid_dpop_proof`/`use_dpop_nonce`) returns the `{error, error_description}` shape. Works in every lifecycle state (takedown-then-sweep composes); idempotent (repeat = 200 of zeros); unknown DID → 404, checked after auth so there is no DID-presence oracle. Rowid-cursor pagination (`limit` default 50 max 100) plus exact-match `action`/`actor`/`subject` filters (an unknown `action` word → 400, like the account listing's `status`). The PUT validates the base32 v2 share envelope structurally and requires index 2 (Custos never holds any other share), then stores only the master-KEK AES-256-GCM wrapping of the 42 envelope bytes (`crypto::encrypt_secret_bytes`, the shared `SecretFamily` format — deliberately no per-row AAD divergence) and appends the `deposited`/`rotated`/`deleted` `recovery_audit_events` row in the same transaction. ## Metrics

The federation-health instrument set served by `GET /metrics`. Names and label keys are
constants in `metrics::names` — **this table mirrors that module; change them together.**
Counters are constructed *without* the `_total` suffix (the Prometheus exporter appends it;
a unit test in `metrics.rs` pins the rendered names). All instruments record through the
typed `AppState.metrics` handle; when `[telemetry] metrics_enabled = false` the same handle
drops measurements at the SDK boundary, so call sites never branch.

| Rendered name | Type | Labels | Recorded by |
|---|---|---|---|
| `http_requests_total` | counter | `route` (matched template or `unmatched`), `status_class` | `metrics::http_metrics_middleware` (outside the rate limiter → 429s count; inside CORS → preflights don't) |
| `firehose_subscribers` | gauge | — | `SubscriberGuard` in `sync_subscribe_repos.rs` (+1 connect, −1 on any exit path) |
| `firehose_events_total` | counter | `frame` (`commit`/`account`/`identity`/`sync`) | `Firehose::broadcast` — the single fan-out choke point |
| `firehose_backfill_window_seconds` | gauge | — | `firehose_gc.rs` after each sweep (age of `MIN(sequenced_at)`; 0 when the log is empty) |
| `firehose_gc_swept_total` / `firehose_gc_last_run_timestamp` | counter / gauge | — | `firehose_gc.rs` after each completed pass |
| `labeler_watch_changes_total` / `labeler_watch_last_run_timestamp` | counter / gauge | — | `labeler_watch.rs` after each completed pass (`changes` = label rows upserted + removed; error early-returns skip the timestamp on purpose — staleness is the alarm) |
| `blob_gc_swept_total` / `blob_gc_last_run_timestamp` | counter / gauge | — | `blob_gc.rs` after each completed pass (a failed-to-start pass leaves the timestamp stale on purpose — that staleness is the alarm) |
| `blob_mirror_synced_total` / `blob_mirror_last_run_timestamp` | counter / gauge | — | `blob_mirror/mod.rs` after each completed pass (`synced` = bucket uploads + deletes; a failed-to-enumerate pass leaves the timestamp stale on purpose — that staleness is the alarm) |
| `blob_scrub_flagged_total` / `blob_scrub_healed_total` / `blob_scrub_last_run_timestamp` | counter / counter / gauge | — | `blob_scrub.rs` after each completed pass (`flagged` = unhealed integrity problems this pass — missing files, hash/size mismatches, orphan files; `healed` = bad/missing files repaired from the blob-mirror bucket; a failed-to-list pass leaves the timestamp stale on purpose). `routes/get_blob.rs` also adds to `flagged` when a serve-time re-hash catches a corrupt file — same alarm channel, so an operator watches one counter |
| `account_reaper_swept_total` / `account_reaper_last_run_timestamp` | counter / gauge | — | `account_reaper.rs` after each completed pass |
| `agent_claim_sweep_swept_total` / `agent_claim_sweep_last_run_timestamp` | counter / gauge | — | `agent_claim_sweep.rs` after each completed pass (error early-returns skip the timestamp on purpose — staleness is the alarm) |
| `admin_nonce_sweep_swept_total` / `admin_nonce_sweep_last_run_timestamp` | counter / gauge | — | `admin_nonce_sweep.rs` after each completed pass |
| `relay_crawl_requests_total` | counter | `outcome` (`ok`/`rejected`/`exhausted`) | `crawler.rs` per finished notification |
| `proxy_requests_total` | counter | `upstream` (`appview`/`chat`/`moderation`/`header_target` — the last for an `app.bsky.*`/`chat.bsky.*` request that used an `atproto-proxy` header to override its default), `status_class` | `app.rs::xrpc_handler` on both the streaming and munged paths |

Cardinality rule: label values are always drawn from small fixed sets or the route table —
never from request data (raw URIs, rkeys, DIDs, hostnames).

## Hard Rules

**Routes must not import from other routes.**
If two routes share logic, that logic belongs in `auth/` (pure) or `db/` (queries). A route
importing from another route creates hidden coupling and makes it impossible to reason about
a handler in isolation.

**Every `.rs` file with runtime behavior must have a pattern comment.**
Add `// pattern: Functional Core`, `// pattern: Imperative Shell`, or
`// pattern: Mixed (unavoidable)` at the top of any file containing functions or
orchestration logic. Files with only types, constants, or re-exports are exempt.

**`db/` submodules own queries, not transactions.**
Business-logic transactions (multi-table atomic operations) live in the route handler or
a dedicated helper called by the handler — not inside `db/` functions. `db/` functions
accept `&SqlitePool` or `&mut SqliteTransaction`; they never open transactions themselves
unless the operation is inherently single-table.

**Authentication must never be cookie-based; permissive CORS on the public surface depends on it.**
`app.rs` applies `CorsLayer::permissive()` to the public surface (landing, `.well-known`, OAuth,
agent registration, all XRPC, static assets) but deliberately **not** to the admin/provisioning
`/v1/*` surface (same-origin only). Permissive CORS is safe only because every auth path is
Bearer/DPoP/signed-request — never an ambient cookie — so a hostile origin cannot ride a logged-in
user's credentials. If any future auth mechanism becomes cookie-based, the permissive CORS layer
must be tightened (explicit origin allowlist + credentials handling) in the same change.

## Adding a New Route

1. Create `src/routes/<name>.rs` with `// pattern: Imperative Shell` at the top.
2. If the handler needs shared auth logic → add to `auth/` (pure) or use an existing extractor.
3. If the handler needs a new DB query → add to the appropriate `db/` submodule.
4. If it's an XRPC procedure: a JSON input body is parsed with `LexiconInput<T>` (never bare
   `axum::Json<T>`) after vendoring its lexicon document (`crates/pds/lexicons/README.md`); a
   no-input procedure takes `NoInputBody` instead. Both must be the handler's final extractor.
5. Register in `src/app.rs` router.
6. Add a `.bru` file in `bruno/` (see root AGENTS.md).

## Adding a New DB Query

1. Identify the owning entity (`accounts`, `oauth`, etc.).
2. Add the function to the matching `db/<entity>.rs` file.
3. If no matching file exists, create one with `// pattern: Imperative Shell`.
4. Export the function and any new data struct via `db/mod.rs` (`pub mod <entity>;`).

- **V034**: Adds the `account_deletion_tokens` table (same SHA-256-hashed, 1-hour, single-use envelope as `plc_operation_tokens` V033 / `password_reset_tokens` V014): email tokens gating `com.atproto.server.deleteAccount`. `requestAccountDelete` inserts a token (delivery stubbed → logged, pending an outbound-email path); `deleteAccount` consumes it (bound to `(token_hash, did)`, atomic single-use). Query functions live in `account_deletion_tokens.rs`. **Permanent-deletion note:** **no account-keyed FK cascades** — the only `ON DELETE CASCADE` in the schema hangs content-addressed ownership rows off their physical tables (`block_owners.cid`→`blocks`, `blob_owners.cid`→`blobs` since V039), never off `accounts` — so account deletion (`account_delete::purge_account`, shared by `deleteAccount` and the `deleteAfter` reaper) must delete every child row explicitly in FK order, never relying on cascade behavior (`refresh_tokens`→`sessions`; `transfer_audit_events`→`transfers`→`transfer_devices`; then the rest), reclaims on-disk blob files no other account owns (per `blob_owners`, V039), and emits an `#account` (`active=false`, `status="deleted"`) frame — but deliberately leaves `repo_seq` untouched (punching per-DID holes would break cursor-replay density), removes repo block ownership rows without deleting shared global block bytes, and does **not** tombstone the did:plc identity (the PDS holds no rotation key; ADR-0001).
- **V033**: Adds the `plc_operation_tokens` table (same SHA-256-hashed, 1-hour, single-use envelope as `password_reset_tokens` V014): email tokens that authorize `com.atproto.identity.signPlcOperation` on the interop account-migration path (ADR-0002). `requestPlcOperationSignature` inserts a token (delivery stubbed → logged, pending an outbound-email path); `signPlcOperation` consumes it. Only the plaintext's hash is stored; `consume_plc_operation_token` marks it used in one statement bound to `(token_hash, did)` so it can neither be replayed nor spent by another account. Query functions live in `plc_operation_tokens.rs`.
- **V032**: Adds the `reserved_signing_keys` table for `com.atproto.server.reserveSigningKey`: public account-migration clients can reserve a repo signing `did:key` before the destination account row exists. The table stores the encrypted PDS-held private key using the same AES-256-GCM envelope as other signing-key storage; `did` is nullable but UNIQUE when provided, making DID-keyed reservations idempotent while allowing anonymous reservations to be claimed later by returned `id`. Query functions live in `repo_keys.rs`.
- **Takedown enforcement + admin surface** (no new migration — reuses V026's columns): `accounts.rs::set_account_takedown` is the first writer for `taken_down_at`, backing `com.atproto.admin.updateSubjectStatus`/`getSubjectStatus` (`routes/update_subject_status.rs`, `routes/get_subject_status.rs`, admin-authed). The lifecycle-gated lookups that previously keyed on `deactivated_at` alone (`get_session_account`, `resolve_identifier`, `resolve_by_email`, `get_repo_write_state`, `advance_repo_root_if_active`) now also require `suspended_at`/`taken_down_at` IS NULL, so a suspension or takedown closes logins and repo writes exactly like a self-service deactivation — closing the enforcement gap V026 left open.
- **V031**: Adds the `app_passwords` table (WITHOUT ROWID, keyed by `(did, name)`, FK→`accounts`): named credentials for the legacy `createSession` flow. Each row stores the argon2id hash of a generated secret (plaintext surfaced once at creation, never stored) plus a `privileged` flag mirroring atproto's `com.atproto.appPass` vs `com.atproto.appPassPrivileged` scopes. `createSession` verifies a supplied password against the account's app-password hashes when the main password does not match (and for mobile accounts with no main password), issuing an app-pass-scoped access token and tagging the refresh token's dormant `app_password_name` column (introduced V002, rebuilt into the live schema by V006); `refreshSession` reads that column to keep the rotated session app-pass-scoped, and refuses to rotate if the app password has since been revoked. Revocation deletes the row *and* the app password's refresh tokens/sessions. Query functions live in `app_passwords.rs`; the revocation transaction lives in `routes/revoke_app_password.rs`.
- **V030**: Adds transfer completion audit metadata for planned device swaps. `transfers.completed_at` records when an accepted transfer becomes terminal, and `transfer_audit_events` stores an immutable event row for completion. The completion workflow keeps the accepted target `transfer_devices` credential, marks prior transfer-device credentials revoked, deletes all promoted account sessions/refresh tokens for the DID, and writes one audit row in the same transaction.
- **V028**: Adds the `repo_seq` table — the **persistent firehose event log** backing
  `com.atproto.sync.subscribeRepos`. The sequencer (`firehose.rs`) was in-memory only, so `seq`
  reset to 0 and the replay backlog emptied on every restart/redeploy. Each sequenced event (a
  `#commit`, `#account`, `#identity`, or `#sync` frame) is now persisted here *before* being broadcast, so `seq` is
  monotonic across restarts (loaded from `MAX(seq)` on boot) and cursor replay reads missed events
  back out of the log. `seq` is an explicit `INTEGER PRIMARY KEY` (rowid alias for index-backed
  `seq > ?` scans) assigned by the in-process sequencer — **not** `AUTOINCREMENT` — so a failed
  insert doesn't consume a number and leave a hole in the dense prefix replay relies on. `event` is
  the DAG-CBOR payload that reconstructs the wire frame, including the commit's CARv1 `blocks`
  (stored because post-commit GC may have reclaimed the blocks the diff was built from); the record
  `value` is not stored (not on the wire). Append-only at the writer, but bounded by the
  `firehose_gc` retention sweep (`run_firehose_gc` prunes a contiguous prefix `seq ≤ watermark`,
  never the live frontier; `retained_boundary_seq`/`prune_below` do the SQL). Query functions live in
  `firehose_seq.rs`.
- **V027**: Adds the `transfers` table for planned device-swap sessions (`POST /v1/transfer/initiate` and the later accept/complete steps). State machine `pending → accepted → completing → complete`, plus a terminal `expired`. One active transfer per account is enforced by a partial UNIQUE index `idx_transfers_active_did ON transfers(did) WHERE status IN ('pending','accepted','completing')`. Expiry is **not** in the index predicate (SQLite requires deterministic predicates; `datetime('now')` is not), so `transfers.rs::insert_transfer` sweeps any expired active row to `expired` before inserting — a still-active row then trips the index and is reported as `DuplicateActive` (the 409 path). A second partial UNIQUE index `idx_transfers_active_code ON transfers(code) WHERE status IN ('pending','accepted','completing')` keeps the 6-char code (the accept-time lookup key) unique among active transfers; an INSERT that trips it is reported as `CodeCollision`, and `routes/transfer_initiate.rs` regenerates the code and retries (bounded). The two cases are told apart via `unique_violation_column`. FK→`accounts(did)`.
- **V026**: Adds nullable `suspended_at` and `taken_down_at` TEXT columns to `accounts` — the moderation-lifecycle signals `com.atproto.sync.getRepoStatus`/`listRepos` report beyond user-initiated `deactivated_at`. Status is derived, not stored (matching `deactivated_at`/`claim_codes`): `accounts.rs::AccountLifecycle::from_timestamps` collapses the three timestamps to `Active`/`Deactivated`/`Suspended`/`TakenDown` with precedence takendown > suspended > deactivated, feeding `get_repo_status` (handler maps the state to the lexicon `active`/`status`) and `list_repos`' `active` flag. The writer (`set_account_takedown`, backing `com.atproto.admin.updateSubjectStatus`) and full enforcement (repo-write gate, login/session lookups) landed later — see "Takedown enforcement + admin surface" above.
- **V025**: Adds the admin-device data model for the operator companion app — three tables: `admin_pairing_codes` (single-use, short-TTL enrollment codes), `admin_devices` (per-device public keys as `did:key`, with a `scopes` growth hook defaulting to `full`), and `admin_nonces` (seen request nonces for anti-replay, keyed `(device_id, nonce)` so uniqueness is per-device, FK→`admin_devices`). Status is derived, not stored (matching `claim_codes` V004): a pairing code is *pending* while `consumed_at IS NULL AND expires_at > now`; a device is *active* while `revoked_at IS NULL`. Query functions live in `admin_devices.rs`; the pairing/register routes (`routes/admin_devices.rs`) wire the mint/get/consume + insert functions. The signed-request guard (`require_admin` in `auth/guards.rs`) consumes `get_device`/`insert_nonce_if_absent`/`touch_last_seen` (the last bumps `last_seen_at` on a successful device auth). The list/revoke device-management routes (`routes/admin_devices.rs`: `GET /v1/admin/devices`, `POST /v1/admin/devices/:id/revoke`) consume `list_devices`/`revoke_device`/`get_device`.
- **V024**: Adds nullable `delete_after` TEXT column to `accounts` — records the optional `deleteAfter` instant from `com.atproto.server.deactivateAccount` (a requested permanent-deletion time). Set alongside `deactivated_at` on deactivation and cleared on reactivation; the reaper that acts on it is not yet implemented. `deactivated_at` (V008) records *that* an account is deactivated; this records *when it asked to be deleted*.
- **V023**: Adds `account_preferences` table (WITHOUT ROWID, keyed by `did`): a single JSON blob per account holding the user's `app.bsky` preferences array, stored locally on the PDS (user data sovereignty) instead of being proxied to the AppView. `updated_at` tracks the last write; FK→`accounts(did)`.
- **V022**: Adds `iroh_identity` table (WITHOUT ROWID, single-row, keyed by UUID id) storing the PDS's Iroh node Ed25519 secret key, AES-256-GCM encrypted with the signing-key master key (same scheme as `oauth_signing_key` (V012) and `jwt_signing_secret` (V015)). Keeps the PDS's Iroh node id stable across restarts.
- **V014**: Adds `password_reset_tokens` table: `token_hash` TEXT PK (SHA-256 hex digest — plaintext never stored), `did` TEXT (FK→accounts), `expires_at` TEXT (1-hour TTL, SQLite datetime), `used_at` TEXT nullable (set on consumption), `created_at` TEXT; index on `did`
- **V013**: Seeds the identity-wallet as a registered OAuth client (`dev.malpercio.identitywallet`) with native application type, DPoP-bound tokens, and custom URL scheme redirect URI (`dev.malpercio.identitywallet:/oauth/callback`); uses INSERT OR IGNORE for idempotency
- **V012**: Adds nullable `jkt` TEXT column to `oauth_tokens` (DPoP key thumbprint for DPoP-bound refresh tokens); creates `oauth_signing_key` table (WITHOUT ROWID, single-row, stores the server's persistent ES256 keypair with AES-256-GCM-encrypted private key)

## Purpose
Owns SQLite connection lifecycle and schema migration for the PDS's server-level database.
Keeps database concerns out of handler code and provides a reusable pool+migration API
that can later serve per-user SQLite databases (Wave 3/4).

## Contracts
- **Exposes**: `open_pool(url: &str) -> Result<SqlitePool, DbError>`, `run_migrations(pool: &SqlitePool) -> Result<(), DbError>`, `DbError`
- **Guarantees**: Pool uses WAL journal mode and max 1 connection. The schema_migrations bootstrap DDL runs outside any transaction. Pending migrations and their bookkeeping inserts run inside a single transaction per call. Migrations are forward-only and idempotent. `schema_migrations` table tracks applied versions.
- **Expects**: Valid sqlx SQLite URL (e.g. `"sqlite::memory:"`, `"sqlite:path.db"`). Pool must be open before calling `run_migrations`.

## Dependencies
- **Uses**: sqlx (SqlitePool, SqliteConnectOptions), thiserror
- **Used by**: `main.rs` (startup sequence), `app::AppState` (holds the pool), test helpers
- **Boundary**: Handlers never call `open_pool`/`run_migrations` directly; they receive the pool via `AppState.db`

## Key Decisions
- Custom migration runner over sqlx's built-in `migrate!()`: gives control over transaction boundaries and avoids sqlx's `_sqlx_migrations` table
- Single connection pool (`max_connections(1)`): avoids SQLite write contention, sufficient for v0.1
- `open_pool` accepts `&str` (not Config/AppState): keeps the function reusable for future per-user DBs

## Invariants
- Migration SQL files are append-only; never modify an applied migration
- Migration versions are sequential positive integers starting at 1
- WAL mode is always enabled (set via SqliteConnectOptions, not raw PRAGMA)
- Foreign key enforcement is always on (set via SqliteConnectOptions .foreign_keys(true), not raw PRAGMA)

content.thinking: All tests are passing with just one warning to address: the `did` prop is being read non-reactively at initialization, which Svelte 5 flags as `state_referenced_locally`. I need to convert it to use `$derived` so it properly tracks the prop value reactively.

content.text:
0 type errors, 158 tests pass — but `svelte-check` flagged a real reactivity issue in my code. Let me fix it:

`★ Insight ─────────────────────────────────────`
- `const isDidWeb = did.startsWith(...)` reads a `$props()` value at component-init time, which in Svelte 5 captures only the *initial* value — if the parent ever reuses this component instance with a different `did`, the copy branches would render for the wrong identity. `$derived` re-evaluates on prop change.
- This is the same class of runes footgun already recorded in this repo's memory (`$state(new Map())` not being reactive): Svelte 5's reactivity is opt-in per binding, so any prop-derived value that feeds the template must go through `$derived`/`$derived.by`.
`─────────────────────────────────────────────────`

content.content:
# Changelog fragments

Every pull request that changes a shipped surface must add a short Markdown fragment:

```text
changelog.d/<id>.<type>.md
```

- `<id>` is the Linear issue identifier in lowercase (for example, `mm-358`). If a
  change has no Linear issue, use the pull request number (for example, `271`).
- `<type>` is one of `added`, `changed`, `fixed`, `removed`, or `security`.
- The file contains one concise, user- or operator-facing Markdown statement. Do not
  include a heading or bullet marker; the release script supplies both.
- Use more than one fragment when a change belongs in more than one category.

Example (`changelog.d/mm-358.added.md`):

```markdown
Release notes now collect user-visible changes from pull requests automatically.
```

The CI gate requires a fragment when a pull request changes a deployable surface:

- server or shared runtime source under `crates/*/src/`, plus PDS runtime assets;
- either mobile app's frontend, native runtime source, static assets, or Tauri config;
- the public marketing site;
- the deployed MCP surfaces — the stdio Custos MCP server (`tools/mcp/src/`) and the
  credential-forwarding sidecar (`tools/mcp-sidecar/src/`, plus its image/config), which
  ships as a Railway service and re-exports the stdio server's tool surface;
- workspace runtime dependency manifests, the production image/config, or the NixOS
  runtime module.

Documentation, tests, design files, CI configuration, scripts, developer tooling, and
other repository-internal changes do not trigger the presence requirement. Any fragment
that is present is still checked for a valid name and non-empty content.

`just set-version X.Y.Z` groups all fragments into a dated Keep a Changelog release
section in `CHANGELOG.md`, then deletes the consumed fragments. This README remains.

input.content: A did:web identity can now be removed from the wallet. The permanent-removal flow was did:plc-only: the entry point was hidden for a did:web, because behind it the removal always tried to publish a PLC tombstone — an operation a did:web has no directory log for, which would have deleted the account and then stranded the identity in a "retry" state that could never succeed. Removal is now method-aware: a did:web is deleted on its PDS and erased from the device with no PLC step, and the wallet says plainly that the last step — taking the DID's `did.json` off the domain — is yours, since it never had control of that domain.

The permanent-removal flow was did:plc-only: the entry point was hidden for a did:web, because behind it the removal always tried to publish a PLC tombstone — an operation a did:web has no directory log for, which would have deleted the account and then stranded the identity in a "retry" state that could never succeed. Removal is now method-aware: a did:web is deleted on its PDS and erased from the device with no PLC step, and the wallet says plainly that the last step — taking the DID's `did.json` off the domain — is yours, since it never had control of that domain.

input.old_string: Shared core `tombstone_and_wipe` fetches the audit-log head as `prev`, builds+signs a `crypto::build_did_plc_tombstone_op` with `per_did_sign_closure` (self-verified via `verify_plc_tombstone_op`), POSTs it to plc.directory, and ONLY THEN calls `IdentityStore::remove_identity` — the wipe deletes the device key that signs the tombstone, so a submit failure must leave it intact for a retry (the `submit_then_wipe` ordering is unit-tested).
input.new_string: Shared core `retire_and_wipe` is **method-aware** and owns the branch both commands go through: a **did:plc** runs `tombstone_and_wipe` (fetch the audit-log head as `prev`, build+sign a `crypto::build_did_plc_tombstone_op` with `per_did_sign_closure`, self-verified via `verify_plc_tombstone_op`, POST it to plc.directory, and ONLY THEN call `IdentityStore::remove_identity` — the wipe deletes the device key that signs the tombstone, so a submit failure must leave it intact for a retry; the `submit_then_wipe` ordering is unit-tested), while a **did:web** skips the tombstone leg entirely and goes straight to the wipe, never contacting plc.directory, reporting `tombstoneCid: None`. A did:web has no PLC log, so routing it through the tombstone path would 404 on the audit-log fetch and wedge the flow permanently: the account gone and its single-use email code spent, while the wipe — gated behind a submit that can never succeed — never runs and the pending-removal marker never clears, so every launch re-offers a doomed retry. The branch lives in the shared core rather than at the command boundary precisely because `tombstone_identity` (the resume path the marker routes to) reaches the same code; guarding only the entry point would leave the wedge reachable. Retiring a did:web network-wide means removing its `did.json` from the domain — an operator action outside the wallet's control, which the UI states rather than simulating.

lines: - `src/blob_backup.rs` — User-held blob backup (4 Tauri IPC commands — the "Back up media" surface): `get_blob_backup_status(did)` (mirror location + opt-in flag + mirror size), `set_blob_backup_enabled(did, enabled)`, `run_blob_backup(did)` (incremental sync pass: paginated public `com.atproto.sync.listBlobs` → diff against the manifest → `getBlob` with Content-Type capture → **recompute the CIDv1 raw-codec SHA-256 CID and compare before writing** → atomic temp-file+rename write into `{root}/blobs/{cid}` → append to the per-DID manifest `{root}/manifests/{sanitized-did}.json` (`cid, mimeType, size, fetchedAt`), saved after every blob so an interrupted run resumes; per-blob failures land in the report, never abort the run), and `restore_blob_backup(did)` (walk the manifest, re-verify each file's hash, `uploadBlob` with the stored MIME type over a `SessionProvider::full_access_client` session — `NeedsUnlock` maps to `SESSION_LOCKED`, the biometric-`sovereignLogin` retry cue; an undownloaded iCloud placeholder or corrupt file is a per-blob failure with guidance). The mirror root resolves: `EZPDS_BLOB_BACKUP_DIR` env override (tests/dev) → the iCloud Drive ubiquity container `Documents/` on iOS (`NSFileManager.URLForUbiquityContainerIdentifier` via `objc2-foundation`, iOS-only target dep; user-visible in the Files app) → on a real device with iCloud off, `BACKUP_UNAVAILABLE` (never a silent local fallback) → elsewhere (macOS/simulator) a local app-data dir reported as `location: "local"`. A corrupt manifest is fail-closed (`MANIFEST_CORRUPT`, file preserved — it may be the only record of MIME types for bytes the PDS has lost). `BlobBackupError` (BACKUP_UNAVAILABLE, SESSION_LOCKED, RATE_LIMITED, IDENTITY_NOT_FOUND, PLC_DIRECTORY_ERROR, SERVER_ERROR, NETWORK_ERROR, STORAGE_ERROR, MANIFEST_CORRUPT, KEYCHAIN_ERROR)

- `src/repo_backup.rs` — User-held repo backup (4 Tauri IPC commands — the "Back up your posts" section of the Media Backup screen, sibling of `blob_backup.rs`): `get_repo_backup_status(did)` (location + opt-in flag + snapshot size/rev), `set_repo_backup_enabled(did, enabled)`, `run_repo_backup(did)` (a full-CAR snapshot pass: `discover_pds` → `PdsClient::fetch_repo_car` over public `com.atproto.sync.getRepo` (`auth: none`, no session) → **validate the CAR client-side** (framing + every block hashing to its CID + exactly one root + a signed commit `version==3` bound to this DID + an intact MST walk — the client twin of `repo-engine`'s `car_import`, using the pure `cid`/`ipld-core`/`serde_ipld_dagcbor` primitives, NOT the repo-engine crate; the MST walk follows subtree + record-value links but never descends into records, since records link to out-of-CAR blobs) → atomic temp-file+rename write into `{root}/repo/{sanitized-did}.car` + a versioned manifest `{root}/repo/{sanitized-did}.json` (`rootCid, rev, sizeBytes, lastBackupAt`); idempotent — an unchanged `rev` skips the CAR rewrite and only advances the timestamp), and `export_repo_backup(did)` (read + **re-validate** the stored CAR; returns `{rootCid, rev, sizeBytes, lastBackupAt, carBase64}` for a caller to import — there is deliberately no "push to my live PDS" button, since `importRepo` needs a *deactivated* account, so restore flows through the migration machinery). A `pub(crate) mirror_repo_car(root, did) -> Option<Vec<u8>>` helper (the repo twin of `blob_backup::mirror_fallback_blob`, fail-closed re-validation) is the iCloud-mirror repo source consumed both by the normal outbound migration's `migration_orchestrator::transfer_repo` (source-`getRepo`-failure fallback) and by the sovereign disaster-recovery flow (`disaster_recovery::recovery_transfer_repo`). Reuses `blob_backup::resolve_backup_root`/`BackupLocation`/`sanitize_did` and the shared ubiquity container (no new entitlement). No encryption (the repo is public data on an `auth: none` endpoint) and, unlike the blob restore, no session — so `RepoBackupError` has **no `SESSION_LOCKED`**: (BACKUP_UNAVAILABLE, RATE_LIMITED, IDENTITY_NOT_FOUND, PLC_DIRECTORY_ERROR, SERVER_ERROR, NETWORK_ERROR, STORAGE_ERROR, MANIFEST_CORRUPT, CAR_INVALID, KEYCHAIN_ERROR)

- `src/recovery.rs` — Recovery override module: `build_recovery_override(pds_client, did, unauthorized_op_cid) -> Result<SignedRecoveryOp, RecoveryError>` (fetches audit log, identifies fork point, builds counter-operation restoring pre-unauthorized state, signs with per-DID device key), `submit_recovery_override(pds_client, did, signed_op) -> Result<ClaimResult, RecoveryError>` (POSTs to plc.directory, updates cached log and DID doc); Tauri IPC commands: `build_recovery_override_cmd`, `submit_recovery_override_cmd`. Types: `SignedRecoveryOp` { diff, signed_op }, `RecoveryState` { did, signed_op }, `RecoveryError` (RECOVERY_WINDOW_EXPIRED, SIGNING_FAILED, PLC_DIRECTORY_ERROR, NETWORK_ERROR, IDENTITY_NOT_FOUND, UNAUTHORIZED_CHANGE_NOT_FOUND)

-- `src/identity_removal.rs` — Permanent identity removal (5 Tauri IPC commands): `request_identity_removal(did)` (gets a full-access session via `SessionProvider::full_access_client` — a `NeedsUnlock` maps to `SessionRequired` so the UI runs `sovereignLogin` first — then calls `com.atproto.server.requestAccountDelete`, which emails a single-use code), `confirm_identity_removal(did, password, token)` (calls `deleteAccount` FIRST — a bad password/code is `InvalidToken` with nothing mutated — then persists a durable pending-removal marker and runs `tombstone_and_wipe`), `tombstone_identity(did)` (resume path: tombstone + wipe only, for when `confirm` deleted the account but the tombstone/wipe failed and the single-use code is already spent), and `list_pending_removals()` (the launch-reconciliation source: the DIDs whose post-delete tombstone/wipe never finished), and `forget_identity_locally(did)` (the local-only escape hatch: wipes the DID's Keychain material and clears any pending marker with NO network step, returning `wasLastIdentity`. For an identity whose PDS account no longer exists — deleted from another device, purged server-side, or migrated away — `deleteAccount` can only answer with an opaque 401 indistinguishable from a wrong password (the PDS is not an account-existence oracle, see `crates/pds/src/routes/delete_account.rs`), so the request/confirm flow can never make progress. It deliberately does NOT tombstone the did:plc — the DID may already be retired or now live on another PDS — so it only promises to remove the identity from THIS device; biometric-gated in the frontend). Shared core `retire_and_wipe` is **method-aware** and owns the branch both commands go through: a **did:plc** runs `tombstone_and_wipe` (fetch the audit-log head as `prev`, build+sign a `crypto::build_did_plc_tombstone_op` with `per_did_sign_closure`, self-verified via `verify_plc_tombstone_op`, POST it to plc.directory, and ONLY THEN call `IdentityStore::remove_identity` — the wipe deletes the device key that signs the tombstone, so a submit failure must leave it intact for a retry; the `submit_then_wipe` ordering is unit-tested), while a **did:web** skips the tombstone leg entirely and goes straight to the wipe, never contacting plc.directory, reporting `tombstoneCid: None`. A did:web has no PLC log, so routing it through the tombstone path would 404 on the audit-log fetch and wedge the flow permanently: the account gone and its single-use email code spent, while the wipe — gated behind a submit that can never succeed — never runs and the pending-removal marker never clears, so every launch re-offers a doomed retry. The branch lives in the shared core rather than at the command boundary precisely because `tombstone_identity` (the resume path the marker routes to) reaches the same code; guarding only the entry point would leave the wedge reachable. Retiring a did:web network-wide means removing its `did.json` from the domain — an operator action outside the wallet's control, which the UI states rather than simulating. **Post-delete recovery marker:** the instant `deleteAccount` succeeds, `confirm_identity_removal` records the DID in the durable `pending-removals` Keychain index (a JSON array), *before* the tombstone's network round trip — the step iOS is most likely to interrupt by suspending the app. Both `confirm_identity_removal` and `tombstone_identity` clear the marker (best-effort) once `tombstone_and_wipe` completes. On launch the UI calls `list_pending_removals()` and, for any listed DID, resumes straight to the idempotent tombstone retry rather than the request flow — which would fail against the already-deleted account. No PDS/DB changes: both `requestAccountDelete`/`deleteAccount` endpoints already exist, and the did:plc tombstone is the DID-level network messaging the PDS can't do (it holds no rotation key, ADR-0001). Types: `RemovalOutcome` { tombstoneCid, wasLastIdentity }, `RemovalError` (SESSION_REQUIRED, REQUEST_DELETE_FAILED, INVALID_TOKEN, ACCOUNT_DELETE_FAILED, INVALID_AUDIT_LOG, TOMBSTONE_SIGNING_FAILED, PLC_DIRECTORY_ERROR, IDENTITY_NOT_FOUND, LOCAL_WIPE_FAILED, RATE_LIMITED, NETWORK_ERROR)

- `src/migrate.rs` — Self-signed account-migration identity leg (ADR-0002 path 1): builds and locally device-key-signs the DID-repointing PLC op and submits it directly to plc.directory — no email token, no `signPlcOperation` round-trip. `build_migration_op(pds_client, dest_client, did) -> Result<SignedMigrationOp, MigrateError>` (fetches audit log for `prev` + current state, reads `getRecommendedDidCredentials` from the DESTINATION PDS via the passed-in authed `OAuthClient`, assembles the op with the device key preserved at `rotationKeys[0]`, runs the strict pre-sign guard, signs with the per-DID device key), `submit_migration_op(pds_client, did, signed_op) -> Result<ClaimResult, MigrateError>` (POSTs to plc.directory, refreshes cached log + DID doc); Tauri IPC commands: `build_migration_op_cmd`, `submit_migration_op_cmd`. - `src/migration_orchestrator.rs` — wallet-authorized outbound migration state machine (ADR-0002 path 1). A corrupt manifest is fail-closed (`MANIFEST_CORRUPT`, file preserved — it may be the only record of MIME types for bytes the PDS has lost). `BlobBackupError` (BACKUP_UNAVAILABLE, SESSION_LOCKED, RATE_LIMITED, IDENTITY_NOT_FOUND, PLC_DIRECTORY_ERROR, SERVER_ERROR, NETWORK_ERROR, STORAGE_ERROR, MANIFEST_CORRUPT, KEYCHAIN_ERROR)

- `src/repo_backup.rs` — User-held repo backup (4 Tauri IPC commands — the "Back up your posts" section of the Media Backup screen, sibling of `blob_backup.rs`): `get_repo_backup_status(did)` (location + opt-in flag + snapshot size/rev), `set_repo_backup_enabled(did, enabled)`, `run_repo_backup(did)` (a full-CAR snapshot pass: `discover_pds` → `PdsClient::fetch_repo_car` over public `com.atproto.sync.getRepo` (`auth: none`, no session) → **validate the CAR client-side** (framing + every block hashing to its CID + exactly one root + a signed commit `version==3` bound to this DID + an intact MST walk — the client twin of `repo-engine`'s `car_import`, using the pure `cid`/`ipld-core`/`serde_ipld_dagcbor` primitives, NOT the repo-engine crate; the MST walk follows subtree + record-value links but never descends into records, since records link to out-of-CAR blobs) → atomic temp-file+rename write into `{root}/repo/{sanitized-did}.car` + a versioned manifest `{root}/repo/{sanitized-did}.json` (`rootCid, rev, sizeBytes, lastBackupAt`); idempotent — an unchanged `rev` skips the CAR rewrite and only advances the timestamp), and `export_repo_backup(did)` (read + **re-validate** the stored CAR; returns `{rootCid, rev, sizeBytes, lastBackupAt, carBase64}` for a caller to import — there is deliberately no "push to my live PDS" button, since `importRepo` needs a *deactivated* account, so restore flows through the migration machinery). A `pub(crate) mirror_repo_car(root, did) -> Option<Vec<u8>>` helper (the repo twin of `blob_backup::mirror_fallback_blob`, fail-closed re-validation) is the iCloud-mirror repo source consumed both by the normal outbound migration's `migration_orchestrator::transfer_repo` (source-`getRepo`-failure fallback) and by the sovereign disaster-recovery flow (`disaster_recovery::recovery_transfer_repo`). Reuses `blob_backup::resolve_backup_root`/`BackupLocation`/`sanitize_did` and the shared ubiquity container (no new entitlement). No encryption (the repo is public data on an `auth: none` endpoint) and, unlike the blob restore, no session — so `RepoBackupError` has **no `SESSION_LOCKED`**: (BACKUP_UNAVAILABLE, RATE_LIMITED, IDENTITY_NOT_FOUND, PLC_DIRECTORY_ERROR, SERVER_ERROR, NETWORK_ERROR, STORAGE_ERROR, MANIFEST_CORRUPT, CAR_INVALID, KEYCHAIN_ERROR)

- `src/recovery.rs` — Recovery override module: `build_recovery_override(pds_client, did, unauthorized_op_cid) -> Result<SignedRecoveryOp, RecoveryError>` (fetches audit log, identifies fork point, builds counter-operation restoring pre-unauthorized state, signs with per-DID device key), `submit_recovery_override(pds_client, did, signed_op) -> Result<ClaimResult, RecoveryError>` (POSTs to plc.directory, updates cached log and DID doc); Tauri IPC commands: `build_recovery_override_cmd`, `submit_recovery_override_cmd`. Types: `SignedRecoveryOp` { diff, signed_op }, `RecoveryState` { did, signed_op }, `RecoveryError` (RECOVERY_WINDOW_EXPIRED, SIGNING_FAILED, PLC_DIRECTORY_ERROR, NETWORK_ERROR, IDENTITY_NOT_FOUND, UNAUTHORIZED_CHANGE_NOT_FOUND)

-- `src/identity_removal.rs` — Permanent identity removal (5 Tauri IPC commands): `request_identity_removal(did)` (gets a full-access session via `SessionProvider::full_access_client` — a `NeedsUnlock` maps to `SessionRequired` so the UI runs `sovereignLogin` first — then calls `com.atproto.server.requestAccountDelete`, which emails a single-use code), `confirm_identity_removal(did, password, token)` (calls `deleteAccount` FIRST — a bad password/code is `InvalidToken` with nothing mutated — then persists a durable pending-removal marker and runs `retire_and_wipe`), `tombstone_identity(did)` (resume path: retire + wipe only, for when `confirm` deleted the account but the tombstone/wipe failed and the single-use code is already spent; for a did:web there is no tombstone to retry, so the resume is the local wipe alone), and `list_pending_removals()` (the launch-reconciliation source: the DIDs whose post-delete tombstone/wipe never finished), and `forget_identity_locally(did)` (the local-only escape hatch: wipes the DID's Keychain material and clears any pending marker with NO network step, returning `wasLastIdentity`. For an identity whose PDS account no longer exists — deleted from another device, purged server-side, or migrated away — `deleteAccount` can only answer with an opaque 401 indistinguishable from a wrong password (the PDS is not an account-existence oracle, see `crates/pds/src/routes/delete_account.rs`), so the request/confirm flow can never make progress. It deliberately does NOT tombstone the did:plc — the DID may already be retired or now live on another PDS — so it only promises to remove the identity from THIS device; biometric-gated in the frontend). Shared core `retire_and_wipe` is **method-aware** and owns the branch both commands go through: a **did:plc** runs `tombstone_and_wipe` (fetch the audit-log head as `prev`, build+sign a `crypto::build_did_plc_tombstone_op` with `per_did_sign_closure`, self-verified via `verify_plc_tombstone_op`, POST it to plc.directory, and ONLY THEN call `IdentityStore::remove_identity` — the wipe deletes the device key that signs the tombstone, so a submit failure must leave it intact for a retry; the `submit_then_wipe` ordering is unit-tested), while a **did:web** skips the tombstone leg entirely and goes straight to the wipe, never contacting plc.directory, reporting `tombstoneCid: None`. A did:web has no PLC log, so routing it through the tombstone path would 404 on the audit-log fetch and wedge the flow permanently: the account gone and its single-use email code spent, while the wipe — gated behind a submit that can never succeed — never runs and the pending-removal marker never clears, so every launch re-offers a doomed retry. The branch lives in the shared core rather than at the command boundary precisely because `tombstone_identity` (the resume path the marker routes to) reaches the same code; guarding only the entry point would leave the wedge reachable. Retiring a did:web network-wide means removing its `did.json` from the domain — an operator action outside the wallet's control, which the UI states rather than simulating. **Post-delete recovery marker:** the instant `deleteAccount` succeeds, `confirm_identity_removal` records the DID in the durable `pending-removals` Keychain index (a JSON array), *before* the tombstone's network round trip — the step iOS is most likely to interrupt by suspending the app. Both `confirm_identity_removal` and `tombstone_identity` clear the marker (best-effort) once `tombstone_and_wipe` completes. On launch the UI calls `list_pending_removals()` and, for any listed DID, resumes straight to the idempotent tombstone retry rather than the request flow — which would fail against the already-deleted account. No PDS/DB changes: both `requestAccountDelete`/`deleteAccount` endpoints already exist, and the did:plc tombstone is the DID-level network messaging the PDS can't do (it holds no rotation key, ADR-0001). 2	//
3	// Permanent identity removal: the wallet-side counterpart to the PDS's
4	// `requestAccountDelete`/`deleteAccount` endpoints plus, for a did:plc, a tombstone.
5	//
6	// A removal has three network/local effects, applied in a strict order:
7	//   1. deleteAccount   — the PDS purges all account data and emits an `#account`
8	//                        (`status="deleted"`) firehose frame relays consume.
9	//                        Method-agnostic.
10	//   2. plc_tombstone   — did:plc ONLY. The wallet signs a tombstone with the DID's
11	//                        device key (rotationKeys[0]) and POSTs it to plc.directory,
12	//                        so the did:plc itself is retired network-wide (the PDS cannot
13	//                        do this — it never holds the rotation key, ADR-0001).
14	//   3. local wipe      — `IdentityStore::remove_identity` deletes every per-DID
15	//                        Keychain entry.
16	//
17	// Ordering invariant: the local wipe runs LAST and only after the tombstone
18	// submits, because the wipe deletes the device key that signs the tombstone. If the
19	// tombstone submit fails, the account is already deleted (its single-use email token
20	// spent) but the device key survives — the UI resumes via `tombstone_identity`, which
21	// retries only the tombstone + wipe.
22	//
23	// Method-awareness (step 2): a did:web has no PLC log and no tombstone operation — it
24	// dies when its document leaves the domain, an operator action outside the wallet's
25	// control. So a non-did:plc removal skips step 2 entirely and goes straight from the
26	// deleteAccount to the local wipe, never contacting plc.directory (whose audit-log fetch
27	// 404s for any DID it does not host). Routing a did:web through the tombstone leg would
28	// wedge the flow permanently: the account would be gone and its single-use email code
29	// spent, while the wipe — gated behind a submit that can never succeed — never runs and
30	// the pending-removal marker never clears, so every launch re-offers a doomed retry. The
31	// branch lives in `retire_and_wipe` rather than at the command boundary because
32	// `tombstone_identity` (the resume path the marker routes to) reaches the same core.

40	/// Keychain account holding the durable "removal in progress (post-delete)" index:
41	/// a JSON array of DIDs whose PDS account was deleted but whose tombstone + local
42	/// wipe has not yet completed. This is the recovery marker that makes a removal
43	/// interrupted after `deleteAccount` (e.g. iOS killing the app mid-tombstone)
44	/// resumable — on launch the UI reconciles any listed DID straight to the
45	/// tombstone-only retry rather than the full request flow (which would fail against
46	/// the already-deleted account).
47	const PENDING_REMOVALS_ACCOUNT: &str = "pending-removals";
48	
49	/// Load the set of DIDs with a pending post-delete removal, propagating a genuine
50	/// Keychain read failure.
51	///
52	/// A missing entry is an empty set, and corrupt JSON reads as empty (the marker is a
53	/// best-effort payload — a decode failure must not wedge the flow). But a real
54	/// Keychain security/IO error is returned, NOT swallowed: the mutators
55	/// (`mark_removal_pending` / `clear_removal_pending`) do a read-modify-write, so
56	/// silently treating a transient read failure as "empty" would let the subsequent
57	/// save overwrite the Keychain and drop any *other* DIDs' pending markers.
58	fn load_pending_removals_strict() -> Result<Vec<String>, crate::keychain::KeychainError> {
59	    match crate::keychain::get_item(PENDING_REMOVALS_ACCOUNT) {
60	        Ok(bytes) => Ok(serde_json::from_slice::<Vec<String>>(&bytes).unwrap_or_else(|e| {
61	            tracing::warn!(error = %e, "pending-removals Keychain entry is not valid JSON; treating as empty");
62	            Vec::new()
63	        })),
64	        Err(e) if crate::keychain::is_not_found(&e) => Ok(Vec::new()),
65	        Err(e) => Err(e),
66	    }
67	}

69	/// Best-effort read of the pending-removal set for the infallible launch check.
70	///
71	/// Any Keychain trouble reads as an empty set — `list_pending_removals` is called
72	/// unconditionally on every launch and must never surface an error that could block it.
73	/// Read-modify-write callers must use [`load_pending_removals_strict`] instead, so a
74	/// transient read failure cannot clobber unrelated markers.
75	fn load_pending_removals() -> Vec<String> {
76	    load_pending_removals_strict().unwrap_or_else(|e| {
77	        tracing::warn!(error = %e, "Keychain error loading pending-removals; treating as empty");
78	        Vec::new()
79	    })
80	}
81	
82	/// Persist the pending-removals set. An empty set deletes the entry entirely so the
83	/// Keychain never carries a stale `[]`.
84	fn save_pending_removals(dids: &[String]) -> Result<(), crate::keychain::KeychainError> {
85	    if dids.is_empty() {
86	        return match crate::keychain::delete_item(PENDING_REMOVALS_ACCOUNT) {
87	            Ok(()) => Ok(()),
88	            Err(e) if crate::keychain::is_not_found(&e) => Ok(()),
89	            Err(e) => Err(e),
90	        };
91	    }
92	    // Vec<String> → JSON is infallible; unwrap keeps the signature Keychain-only.
93	    let json = serde_json::to_vec(dids).expect("Vec<String> always serializes to JSON");
94	    crate::keychain::store_item(PENDING_REMOVALS_ACCOUNT, &json)
95	}

101	fn mark_removal_pending(did: &str) -> Result<(), crate::keychain::KeychainError> {

103	    if !dids.iter().any(|d| d == did) {

cd "$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)" && git add -A && git commit -q -F - <<'EOF'
Wallet: method-aware identity removal for did:web (MM-464)

Permanent identity removal was did:plc-only end to end. The UI gated the
entry point on `did:plc:`, so a did:web identity could not be removed at
all — and that gate was load-bearing: behind it, `confirm_identity_removal`
ran `deleteAccount` (method-agnostic, would succeed) and then always
reached for the plc.directory audit log to chain a tombstone onto, which
404s for any did:web. The account would be gone and its single-use email
code spent, while the local wipe — gated behind a submit that can never
succeed — never ran and the pending-removal marker never cleared, so every
launch re-offered a doomed retry, forever.

Backend: `retire_and_wipe` is the new method-aware core both commands go
through. A did:plc keeps the existing tombstone-then-wipe path (and its
wipe-last ordering invariant); anything else goes straight to the local
wipe, never contacting plc.directory, and reports `tombstoneCid: None`.
The branch lives in the shared core rather than at the command boundary
because `tombstone_identity` — the resume path the pending marker routes
to on launch — reaches the same code, so guarding only the entry point
would leave the wedge reachable from an ungated caller.

Frontend: the `did:plc:` condition on `onremove` is dropped, and the
screen branches on the outcome's null `tombstoneCid` rather than on the
DID string alone. A did:web removal drops the "retire on the network by
tombstoning" promise from the warning, withholds the escape hatch's
advanced "also retire on the network" option (it could not do what it
says), and ends in a new `web_epilogue` state naming the document URL to
take down — the same "the wallet can't do this part for you" framing the
did:web ceremony's publish step already uses. Where the server publishes
the document on the account's behalf, deleting the account already stops
it being served, and the epilogue says so.

Tests: did:web removal never contacts plc.directory (asserted against a
catch-all mock with zero calls), the wedge regression (marker clears with
no tombstone, no permanent retry state), idempotent re-wipe, and the null
`tombstoneCid` serialization on both sides of the IPC seam.
EOF
